tools.name: auth
tools.description: CloudBase (Tencent CloudBase) dev-stage login and environment binding. Unsure where to start? Call auth(status) first (read-only, no arguments) to confirm the login state and the current environment. After login you can access cloud resources; an environment (env) is the isolation unit for cloud functions, databases, static hosting, etc. Other MCP tools operate on the bound environment. No environment yet? On the China site a new user can create a trial environment for free, then bind it with set_env. Supports: status, start_auth (login), login_by_api_key, set_env (bind env), logout. auth(status) returns credential_scope (account / single_env API Key) and current region; a single-env API Key can only see its bound envId — missing other-region envs is a permission boundary, not a missing environment. Optional site/region/lang params: site=domestic|intl, region=e.g. ap-shanghai|ap-singapore, lang=zh|en output language.

action.description: Action: status=query status, start_auth=start login, login_by_api_key=log in with an API Key, set_env=bind an environment (pass envId), logout=log out

authMode.description: Authentication mode: device=device-code authorization, web=browser callback authorization

oauthEndpoint.description: Advanced optional setting: custom device-code login endpoint. When configured, oauthCustom defaults to true

clientId.description: Advanced optional setting: custom client_id for device-code login; the default is used when omitted

oauthCustom.description: Advanced optional setting: toggles the custom endpoint response format. Defaults to false without an endpoint and true when an endpoint is configured. Endpoints using the standard {code,result} wrapper format (such as the international-site tcb-api.tencentcloud.com) should explicitly pass false

site.description: Site: domestic=China site, intl=international site. For environments activated on Tencent Cloud International, login (start_auth/login_by_api_key) must explicitly pass intl; otherwise the China-site path is used and international-site environments are not visible. An explicit per-call value takes precedence over the TCB_SITE environment variable, region mapping, and project configuration, and affects the login endpoint, authorization page, and API Key exchange gateway

envId.description: Environment ID (the unique CloudBase environment identifier). After binding, tools operate on this environment. Required when action=set_env

region.description: Region (such as ap-shanghai / ap-guangzhou / ap-singapore). Used for region-to-site inference and API Key exchange gateway selection; an explicit site takes precedence

lang.description: Output language: zh=Chinese (default), en=English. Overrides the instance language (createCloudBaseMcpServer lang option / TCB_LANG / project.json)

apiKey.description: CloudBase API Key; required when action=login_by_api_key

apiKeyEnvId.description: CloudBase environment ID (EnvId); required when action=login_by_api_key to identify the environment the API Key belongs to

reveal.description: Optional when action=get_temp_credentials. true returns plaintext temporary credentials; the default false returns only masked values

tools.name: queryEnv
tools.description:
Query CloudBase environment information: environment list, details of a specific environment, security domains, resource usage and monitoring metrics. For action=list, even when envId is passed, action=list still returns only a summary, never full resource details or expiry. An env-level credential (API Key / hosted authorization token) can only see its bound envId and returns credential_scope=single_env; in that case region plays no part in the query and is reported as such in ignored_params (AppliedFilters.region is null) — do not mistake that for a missing environment or a region filter that failed to apply. To query details of a known EnvId (including resource fields and billing info), you must use action=info and pass the target environment's envId. action=info appends BillingInfo when available (billing fields such as ExpireTime, PayMode, IsAutoRenew).

📊 action=usage returns the billing cycle and per-module resource-point usage, grouped by module.

📈 action=metrics queries time series for env/gateway QPS, cloud function invocations and errors, database CPU/memory/disk, CloudRun CPU/QPS, and more (CloudBase built-in monitoring, not Cloud Monitor GetMonitorData). startTime/endTime use the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss and must be passed as a pair, defaulting to the last 24 hours when omitted; CloudRun Tke* metrics must pass the service name as resourceID. Do not use callCloudApi to guess monitoring Actions.

🔍 action=info also derives three fields used for backend selection (PG environments carry the instance form as well):
- `EnvInfo.RuntimeMode`: 'postgresql' or 'nosql', the backend recommended by default for new work (postgresql when PG is enabled, otherwise nosql).
- `EnvInfo.RuntimeBackends`: the three booleans `{postgresql, nosql, mysql}`, describing the backends that actually coexist in the current environment.
- `EnvInfo.RuntimeModeHints`: the API/tool/skill hints for each backend.
- `EnvInfo.PostgreSQL[].TenantType`: the PG instance form — `SHARED` (SDK / gateway access only) or `DEDICATED` (has the private host / TCP endpoint).

🌐 action=info also returns the route state of the default static domain, `StaticStorages[].staticDomainRouteEnabled` and `EnvInfo.staticDomainRouteEnabled` (same source as queryHosting websiteConfig); `StaticStorages[].StaticDomain` remains the nominal domain. `false` means the default static domain root route is disabled (requests return GATEWAY_ROUTE_DISABLED) — do not treat the nominal domain as a reachable URL.

Before writing business/permission/storage code, AI must check these three items first: in PG mode, new work should prefer `app.rdb()` + RLS (`managePgDatabase action=execute` running `CREATE POLICY`) + pgstore; existing NoSQL collections / legacy storage / `managePermissions(resourceType="noSqlDatabase")` remain valid in a classic PG environment. **Exception (pgdoc)**: when the document-database API is carried by PostgreSQL and client SDK calls stay unchanged, CUSTOM collection security rules do not take effect — use the four basic permissions or move validation into a cloud function. Do not rewrite existing document-database code into `app.rdb()`, and do not assume data was migrated automatically. `RuntimeBackends` lists provisioned resources only; it does not say who carries document requests, so confirm the enablement state with the user. What truly does not apply is MySQL and the data model tools: when `RuntimeBackends.mysql === false`, none of `manageMysqlDatabase` / `queryMysqlDatabase` / the `relational-database-mcp-cloudbase` skill should be used; `manageDataModel` / `modifyDataModel` only work in classic mode and have no PG counterpart.

action.description: Query type: list=environment list/summary filtering (filter by envId / region; no expiry), info=details of a specified environment (envId required; returns resource fields and billing information), domains=security domain list, usage=environment resource usage (envId required), metrics=environment monitoring time series (envId and metricName required)

alias.description: Filter by environment alias. Optional when action=list

aliasExact.description: Filter by exact environment alias, so environments with similar prefixes are not mistaken for candidates. Optional when action=list; used together with alias

envId.description: Environment ID. Optional when action=list (filter only; still returns summaries); required when action=info / usage / metrics; optional when action=domains (omit it to query the currently bound environment).

region.description: Query region. Only effective when action=list; account-level credentials query that region. Environment-level credentials (API Key / hosted authorization token) ignore this parameter and always return the bound environment — do not infer that the region has no environment. ⚠️ ap-singapore belongs to both the China and international sites; without an explicit site it is queried as international (site=intl). To query the China site, run auth(site="domestic") or set TCB_SITE=domestic first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Optional when action=list

type.description: Usage module filter (same set as the console usage page). Only effective when action=usage; omitting it queries all modules. WARNING: passing it narrows the query to those modules, so `credits.total` is omitted and the panel stops judging sufficiency; the plan is still returned. Omit this parameter to compare against the full quota.

startDate.description: Usage start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Only effective when action=usage; must be paired with endDate. When omitted, the current billing cycle is used.

endDate.description: Usage end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Only effective when action=usage; must be paired with startDate. When omitted, the current billing cycle is used.

needUsageDetails.description: Whether to return four levels of usage detail. Only effective when action=usage; defaults to false, which returns the module level only (Module, CreditsValue as total spend, DeductValue as plan-included usage) plus DailyTotals for the last 7 days, a few hundred characters. true returns module -> metric -> resource type (ResourceType) -> day (ValueDetailList[].CalcTime), about 50k characters for all modules; pass it only when reconciling day by day. Metric names are raw API codes (Capacity / Flux / CU / InputToken.<model>): when explaining them to a user, translate into plain words for the module (capacity, traffic, invocation count, model input tokens) instead of reading the code out; if unsure, say it is an API field name rather than guessing. The finest granularity is metric x day: there is no per-request trail, and no money or unit price.

metricName.description: Monitoring metric name. Required and only effective when action=metrics. GatewayTraceEnvQPS/EnvQPSAll=environment and gateway QPS; FunctionInvocation/FunctionError/FunctionTimeout/FunctionThrottle=function invocations, errors, timeouts, and throttling; DbRead/DbWrite/DbSizepkg=document database reads, writes, and capacity; MysqlCpuUsageRate/MysqlMemoryUse/MysqlStorageUsage=SQL database CPU, memory, and disk; TkeCpuUsedService/TkeQPSService/TkeHttpErrorService=CloudRun CPU, QPS, and errors.

startTime.description: Monitoring start time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss). Only effective when action=metrics; must be paired with endTime. Defaults to the last 24 hours when omitted. The end time must be at least five minutes later than the start time.

endTime.description: Monitoring end time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss). Only effective when action=metrics; must be paired with startTime. Defaults to the last 24 hours when omitted.

period.description: Aggregation period in seconds. Only effective when action=metrics; when omitted, the backend selects it from the time range. 86400 cannot be used for ranges of 1 day or less; 300 cannot be used for ranges over 3 days.

resourceID.description: Resource ID. Only effective when action=metrics. Pass a function name for cloud functions, a collection name for the document database, and a service name for CloudRun. GatewayTraceEnvQPS uses the environment-level all|:|all|:|all|:|all when omitted.

subresourceID.description: Subresource ID. Only effective when action=metrics; pass the version name when querying monitoring data for a specific CloudRun version.

tools.name: envDomainManagement
tools.description:
⚠️ DEPRECATED: This tool is deprecated and has been folded into manageEnv. Use manageEnv(action="addSecurityDomain") / manageEnv(action="removeSecurityDomain") instead (the domains parameter is identical). This alias will be removed in the next version.

Manages [environment security domains] = the browser cross-origin (CORS) allowlist: it controls which web origins (host:port) may call this environment's CloudBase resources directly from the browser. It only performs CORS origin validation; it does not provide an access domain and does not involve HTTPS certificates. ⚠️ This is completely independent from [gateway custom domains] — the two are unrelated: to bind your own domain as an HTTPS access entry (CloudRun / gateway service), that is manageGateway's job — first queryGateway(listCustomDomains); if a domain already exists, use manageGateway(createRoute) with an explicit domain (no certificate needed); only use bindCustomDomain when binding a brand-new domain for the first time (certificateId required). Do not use this tool for that.

Usage guidance: (the original tool names createEnvDomain/deleteEnvDomain may still be used for compatibility with older AI rules) when a browser web app needs to access CloudBase resources directly from a local Vite / dev server, first use queryEnv(action=domains) to check whether the host:port of the actual current browser origin is already in the allowlist, then add that actual value. After adding or deleting, poll queryEnv(action=domains) about every 10 seconds to confirm the state has converged; do not sleep a full 10 minutes at once — most environments converge within a few minutes.

action.description: Operation type: create=add a security domain, delete=delete a security domain

domains.description: Security domain array (host:port format, such as localhost:5173 or 127.0.0.1:4173). These are not custom domains and do not require certificates.

tools.name: manageEnv
tools.description:
Manages CloudBase environments. Supports: listPackages=query available packages, create=create a new environment (confirmation required), modifyPlan=change the package (upgrade/downgrade, confirmation required), renew=renew the environment (confirmation required), addSecurityDomain=add an environment security domain (browser CORS allowlist, not billed, no confirmation needed), removeSecurityDomain=remove an environment security domain (not billed, no confirmation needed).

⚠️ For billed operations (create/modifyPlan/renew) you must show the configuration summary and wait for the user to confirm with confirm="yes" before executing; security domain operations (addSecurityDomain/removeSecurityDomain) are not billed and need no confirm.

ℹ️ A security domain = the browser cross-origin (CORS) allowlist; it controls which web origins (host:port) may call this environment's CloudBase resources directly from the browser, does not provide an access domain, and does not involve HTTPS certificates. Binding your own domain as an HTTPS access entry (CloudRun/gateway service) is manageGateway's job (listCustomDomains/bindCustomDomain) and is unrelated to this tool.

action.description: Operation type: listPackages=query available packages, create=create an environment, modifyPlan=change the package, renew=renew, addSecurityDomain=add a security domain (CORS allowlist entry), removeSecurityDomain=delete a security domain

domains.description: Security domain array (host:port format, such as localhost:5173 or 127.0.0.1:4173). Required and only effective when action=addSecurityDomain/removeSecurityDomain. These are CORS allowlist entries, not custom domains, and do not require certificates. Before adding one, use queryEnv(action=domains) to check whether the browser's actual origin is already in the allowlist.

alias.description: Environment alias (required when action=create). Must contain lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens; cannot start or end with a hyphen; maximum 20 characters

packageId.description: Package ID (required when action=create/modifyPlan). Take the PackageName returned by manageEnv(action="listPackages") — those are the packages selectable in the new-purchase / new-environment menus (baas_personal, baas_pf_standard, baas_pf_enterprise, baas_pf_enterprise_senior, baas_trial, baas_integration). The platform still accepts other valid packageIds (legacy package families, whitelisted ones), so take the actual creation result as authoritative. Available packages differ per site, so do not fill it in from memory.

resources.description: Resource types to enable (optional when action=create). Allowed values: storage, function, postgresql; defaults to all three when omitted. CreateEnv requires Resources to be non-empty, so MCP always sends this field. flexdb (document database) is no longer included: creating an environment does not create a NoSQL instance; its availability is reported by EnvInfo.RuntimeBackends from queryEnv(action="info").

duration.description: Purchase or renewal duration in months. Optional when action=create/renew; defaults to 1

externalStorage.description: Shared COS bucket configuration for cloud storage (optional when action=create). Passing this object means the environment does not get its own dedicated COS bucket; it uses the given bucket as its cloud storage medium and is isolated from other environments in the same bucket by basePath. It applies to cloud storage only — the static hosting bucket is allocated by the platform when hosting is enabled. All three fields are required. ⚠️ Like region, the confirming call (confirm="yes") reads only its own arguments, so omitting it there silently creates the environment with a dedicated bucket.

region.description: Region of the shared bucket, for example ap-shanghai

basePath.description: Base path prefix. Must be unique within the shared bucket; isolates this environment from others in the same bucket

region.description: Creation region (only effective when action=create). Passed through with X-TC-Region semantics and determines where the new environment is created; CLI equivalent: tcb env create --region ap-shanghai. When omitted, the current session region is used (cloudBaseOptions.region → TCB_REGION → project configuration / rc binding → site default: ap-shanghai for the China site, ap-singapore for the international site). region is not written into the CreateEnv request body; it takes effect through the request-layer region context, matching the callCloudApi contract not to put Region in params. ⚠️ ap-singapore belongs to both the China and international sites; without an explicit site it is inferred as international (site=intl). To create there on the China site, first use auth(site="domestic") or set TCB_SITE=domestic.

confirm.description: Confirm the operation. All billed operations (create/modifyPlan/renew) require passing "yes"

tools.name: readNoSqlDatabaseStructure
tools.description: Read CloudBase NoSQL database collection and index structures. Supports listing collections, describing a collection, listing indexes, and checking index existence. This is a server-side management tool for querying database structure from the admin side, not for writing client code.

action.description:
listCollections: List collections
describeCollection: Describe collection details (including an index summary)
checkCollection: Check whether a collection exists
listIndexes: List indexes for a specified collection
checkIndex: Check whether a specified index exists

limit.description: Maximum number of results (optional for listCollections)

collectionName.description: Collection name (required for describeCollection, listIndexes, and checkIndex)

tools.name: writeNoSqlDatabaseStructure
tools.description: Create, delete, and manage CloudBase NoSQL database collections. Supports creating new collections, deleting existing collections, and adding/removing indexes via updateCollection's updateOptions.CreateIndexes / updateOptions.DropIndexes. Use action=createCollection to create a new collection. This is a server-side management tool for operating collection and index structures from the admin side, not for writing client code.

action.description:
createCollection: Create a collection
updateCollection: Update collection configuration; pass updateOptions.CreateIndexes to add indexes and updateOptions.DropIndexes to remove indexes
deleteCollection: Delete a collection

updateOptions.description: Update options for updateCollection. CreateIndexes adds indexes and DropIndexes removes indexes.

IndexName.description: Name of the index to create

Direction.description: Index direction; 1 usually means ascending and -1 means descending

MgoIndexKeys.description: Index field list supporting single-field and compound indexes

MgoKeySchema.description: Field and constraint configuration for the index to create

IndexName.description: Name of the index to remove

tools.name: readNoSqlDatabaseContent
tools.description: Query data records in the CloudBase NoSQL database. Supports filtering, pagination, and sorting for admin-side data queries and operations.limit defaults to 100 with a maximum of 1000; use offset pagination beyond that.projection only supports a { field: 1|0 } object (example {"_id":1,"name":1,"createdAt":1}); do not pass field arrays.

instanceId.description: Optional explicit database instance ID; when omitted, it is resolved and cached automatically

query.description: Query condition as an object or string; an object is recommended

projection.description: Return-field projection. Only an object or equivalent JSON string is supported, and values must be 1/0/true/false. Valid examples: {"_id":1,"name":1,"createdAt":1} (include) or {"password":0} (exclude). Do not pass field arrays such as ["name","age"], and do not mix inclusion and exclusion except for _id.

sort.description: Sort condition. Only an array such as [{"key":"createdAt","direction":-1}] or the equivalent JSON string is supported.

limit.description: Maximum number of results; an integer from 1 to 1000, defaulting to 100. Values above 1000 are rejected by the Cloud API MgoLimit lte validation; use offset pagination.

tools.name: writeNoSqlDatabaseContent
tools.description: Modify data records in the CloudBase NoSQL database. Supports insert, update (with $set/$inc/$push and other operators), delete, upsert, and more for admin-side data writes and operations.⚠️ Server-side writes do not include _openid: if the collection relies on client-side SDK (@cloudbase/js-sdk or WeChat Mini Program wx.cloud.database()) row-level security rules (e.g. doc._openid == auth.openid), you must manually add the _openid field on server-side writes, or clients will not be able to read the data.⚠️ Partial updates of nested fields must use dot paths, e.g. `$set: {"shipping.city": "guangzhou"}`; passing a nested object directly overwrites the whole field.

action.description:
insert: Insert data (add documents)
update: Update data
delete: Delete data

instanceId.description: Optional explicit database instance ID; when omitted, it is resolved and cached automatically

documents.description: Array of document objects to insert; each document must be an object (required for insert)

query.description: Query condition as an object or string; an object is recommended (required for update/delete)

update.description:
Update content as an object or string; an object is recommended (required for update). Pass MgoUpdate using MongoDB update semantics: for partial updates, use operators such as `$set`, `$inc`, `$unset`, and `$push`, for example `$set` to update `status`. Do not pass a plain field-to-value object directly, because it may replace the entire document.

⚠️ Nested fields must use dot notation (such as `shipping.city`); replacing the whole object is prohibited:
- ❌ Incorrect: { "$set": { "shipping": { "city": "guangzhou" } } } — replaces all of shipping and loses existing fields such as address and province
- ✅ Correct: { "$set": { "shipping.city": "guangzhou" } } — updates only city and preserves other fields under shipping

isMulti.description: Whether to update multiple records (optional for update/delete)

upsert.description: Whether to insert when no record exists (optional for update)

tools.name: manageDataModel
tools.description: Data model query tool that supports querying and listing data models (read-only). Distinguish operations via the action parameter: list=get the model list (without Schema, optional names parameter for filtering), get=query a single model's details (including Schema field list, formats, relations, etc.; requires the name parameter), docs=generate SDK usage documentation (requires the name parameter)

action.description: Operation type: get=query a single model (including its Schema field list, formats, and relations; requires the name parameter), list=get the model list (without Schema; optional names parameter for filtering), docs=generate SDK usage documentation (requires the name parameter)

name.description: Name of the data model to query. This parameter is required when action='get' or action='docs' and must identify an existing data model. Use action='list' to obtain available model names

names.description: Array of model names, optionally used to filter the list operation

tools.name: modifyDataModel
tools.description: Create data models from a Mermaid classDiagram. For compatibility, the tool name remains modifyDataModel; currently only creating new models is supported, not updating existing model structures. Includes async task monitoring that polls automatically until completion or timeout.

mermaidDiagram.description:
Mermaid classDiagram code describing the data model structure.
Example:
classDiagram
    class Student {
        name: string <<Name>>
        age: number = 18 <<Age>>
        gender: x-enum = "Male" <<Gender>>
        classId: string <<Class ID>>
        identityId: string <<Identity ID>>
        course: Course[] <<Courses>>
        required() ["name"]
        unique() ["name"]
        enum_gender() ["Male", "Female"]
        display_field() "name"
    }
    class Class {
        className: string <<Class name>>
        display_field() "className"
    }
    class Course {
        name: string <<Course name>>
        students: Student[] <<Students>>
        display_field() "name"
    }
    class Identity {
        number: string <<Document number>>
        display_field() "number"
    }

    %% Relationships
    Student "1" --> "1" Identity : studentId
    Student "n" --> "1" Class : student2class
    Student "n" --> "m" Course : course
    Student "n" <-- "m" Course : students
    %% Class names
    note for Student "Student model"
    note for Class "Class model"
    note for Course "Course model"
    note for Identity "Identity model"

action.description: Operation type: create=create a new model

publish.description: Whether to publish the model immediately

dbInstanceType.description: Database instance type: MySQL database or document database (NoSQL)

tools.name: queryPgDatabase
tools.description:
⚠️ Read-only tool: only accepts read-only SQL such as SELECT. CREATE / ALTER / DROP / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE are rejected outright (and a 42703/42P01 usually means a guessed table or column name — run action=objects to see the real structure instead of assuming names like schema_migrations). For writes and DDL use managePgDatabase: action=execute for DML/GRANT/RLS, action=applyMigration for schema changes.

Query the CloudBase PostgreSQL database: get the current PG context, list schema-qualified database objects, read lightweight metadata, inspect a single object schema, and run read-only SQL.

action.description: Action type: context=get the current PostgreSQL context; objects=list schema-qualified database objects; metadata=get lightweight table metadata; schema=inspect a single schema-qualified object structure; sql=run read-only SQL

objectName.description: Schema-qualified PostgreSQL object name used when action=schema, e.g. public.users

schema.description: Optional schema filter, used with action=objects or action=metadata

limit.description: Optional cap on summary size, applied to objects, metadata, or SQL result rows. Defaults to 20, maximum 200.

tools.name: managePgDatabase
tools.description: Manage CloudBase PostgreSQL: run confirmed write SQL, pre-check SQL risk, manage migrations, and manage Realtime settings. Schema changes such as CREATE TABLE/ALTER/DROP must use applyMigration (explicit migrationVersion; the local cloudbase/migrations/<version>_<name>.sql file is written or verified automatically before success, matching the CLI tcb db pg migration). Do not use execute by default. execute is mainly for DML and ops SQL such as GRANT/RLS. Three Realtime actions: describeRealtime reads the settings (the response has no provisioning flag, so success does not mean Realtime is provisioned); enableRealtime provisions and resumes the service, equivalent to setting Suspend=false (the first call on an unprovisioned environment provisions it automatically, and it is a no-op when already provisioned and not suspended); modifyRealtime applies an incremental update from the fields you pass explicitly (requires confirm=true, and changing suspend immediately drops all live WebSocket connections of the environment, globally).

action.description: Action type. For everyday writes use execute (DML/GRANT/RLS; schema DDL is rejected by default and needs allowDdlViaExecute=true) or dryRun (analyze only, no execution). CREATE TABLE / schema changes must use applyMigration — see the tool description for the full flow (polling, timeout, landed-in-history check). The other six support migrations: planMigration=preview, listMigrations=list applied, migrationDetail=one record, describeMigrationTask=inspect a Push task, fetchMigration=pull remote SQL locally, repairMigration=fix history. plan / apply / repair all need migrationName + migrationVersion; migrationDetail needs only migrationVersion. describeRealtime / enableRealtime / modifyRealtime manage Realtime (see the tool description).

sql.description: SQL statement used when action=execute, dryRun, planMigration, applyMigration, or repairMigration(applied)

confirm.description: Must be explicitly set to true before running any write SQL (execute etc.) and for action=modifyRealtime; when modifyRealtime omits it nothing is sent and the tool returns the current values plus the pending changes so you can confirm with the user first.

envId.description: Optional CloudBase environment ID; the current MCP environment is used when omitted.

instanceId.description: Optional PostgreSQL logical instance identifier, defaults to cloudbase-pg.

defaultSchema.description: Optional default schema, defaults to public.

role.description: Optional PostgreSQL role, passed as Role to the Manager SDK executePGSql (the platform issues SET ROLE). Defaults to cloudbase_postgres. Recommended values: cloudbase_postgres / anon / authenticated / service_role. Do not pass postgres, postgres_pgdb_*, platform-reserved roles (the platform management account, not exposed to users), or roles invented from the environment name; when unsure omit this field, or first run SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles with cloudbase_postgres.

objectName.description: Optional object name, currently only used for non-migration scenarios. For migration actions use migrationName / migrationVersion instead.

migrationName.description: Required for plan/apply/repair: migration name starting with a lowercase letter, containing only lowercase letters and underscores (no digits — the server-side PushPGUserMigrations rejects names containing digits).

migrationVersion.description: 14-digit timestamp YYYYMMDDHHMMSS. Required for plan/apply/detail/repair; optional for fetchMigration (passing it pulls only that record, omitting it pulls the full remote history). It must never be generated silently by the server, to avoid diverging from the local cloudbase/migrations/<version>_<name>.sql file. applyMigration is not incremental: send the complete SQL every time; when a task fails terminally and listMigrations shows the version did not land, that version is not consumed — just pick a new migrationVersion and re-send the full SQL (the same name with a different version does not conflict).

rollbackSql.description: Optional for plan/apply: rollback SQL statement.

limit.description: Optional for list: maximum number of records returned, 1-500, defaults to 100.

offset.description: Optional for list: paging offset, defaults to 0.

lockTimeoutMs.description: Optional for apply: maximum time to acquire the database lock in milliseconds, defaults to 5000.

statementTimeoutMs.description: Optional for apply: maximum execution time per SQL statement in milliseconds, defaults to 300000.

taskPollTimeoutMs.description: Optional for apply: maximum wait while polling DescribeTaskResult, in milliseconds. Defaults to 600000 (10 minutes). Range 5000-600000. After a timeout always call describeMigrationTask(taskId) before listMigrations, and never re-push the same version immediately.

waitForTask.description: Optional for apply, defaults to true. When set to false, Push returns the TaskId immediately (errorCode=MIGRATION_TASK_PENDING) and the caller polls the task to a terminal state with describeMigrationTask, then confirms with listMigrations whether it landed; useful when the MCP host has a short tool-call timeout. The default true waits synchronously for the terminal state.

taskId.description: Required for describeMigrationTask: the TaskId returned by PushPGUserMigrations / applyMigration. Used for a one-shot DescribeTaskResult query (Status/Phase/Reason) without polling.

repairStatus.description: Required for repair: applied=mark as applied (Query can be backfilled), reverted=delete the history record.

repairReason.description: Required for repair: the repair reason.

force.description: Optional for fetchMigration, defaults to false. true=overwrite the existing local SQL file with the same name; false=skip existing files. Use it to realign Git checksums from the remote history.

includeAll.description: Optional for planMigration / applyMigration, defaults to false. true=allow out-of-order versions (older than the remote LatestVersion) to still Preview/Push; use it only when intentionally backfilling or applying out-of-order migrations — normally pick a larger migrationVersion instead.

allowDdlViaExecute.description: Optional, defaults to false. Set it to true only when intentionally bypassing migration history, which is the only case where schema DDL is allowed through execute; normal CREATE TABLE / schema changes must use applyMigration.

suspend.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime (enableRealtime is equivalent to Suspend=false). Global, affects every node of the environment: true immediately drops all live WebSocket connections, rejects new ones (HTTP 403) and disables the server-side broadcast API; false restores the service. Any change of the suspend value triggers one disconnect, so clients must reconnect.

privateOnly.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime: when true only private channels are allowed; clients cannot join channels prefixed with public:.

presenceEnabled.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime: global presence switch. When false, client presence joins on a channel are rejected.

maxConcurrentUsers.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime: maximum concurrent users (multiple connections of the same user count once); new connections are rejected above it. Server-side range 0-15000.

maxEventsPerSecond.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime: maximum broadcast events per second across all clients; exceeding it returns a rate-limit error.

maxJoinsPerSecond.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime: maximum joins per second; new joins are throttled above it.

maxBytesPerSecond.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime: maximum broadcast payload bytes per second across all clients; exceeding it rejects messages.

maxChannelsPerClient.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime: maximum channels per client; a client above it cannot join more channels.

maxPresenceEventsPerSecond.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime: maximum presence events per second across all clients (track/untrack).

maxPayloadSizeInKB.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime: maximum payload size per message in KB; larger messages are rejected.

connectionPool.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime: Realtime database connection pool size used for RLS authorization queries. This is not the PG instance connection pool.

postgresChangesPool.description: Applies to action=modifyRealtime: Realtime dedicated connection pool for CDC (postgres_changes), isolated from the broadcast/auth pool.

objectKeys.description: Multiple object keys for planning object metadata queries

objects.description: Metadata for objects to upload. File bytes are not transferred through MCP.

expiresIn.description: Signed URL validity in seconds, from 60 to 86400.

request.description: Official request payload used by describeCreateResult/describeTaskStatus/describeInstanceSlowQueries/describeInstanceErrorLogs (may include InstanceId, etc.)

dbInstance.description: Optional SQL database instance context for runQuery / slow-query / error-log actions

startTime.description: Slow-query / error-log query start time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss)

endTime.description: Slow-query / error-log query end time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss)

Prefer CloudBase PostgreSQL (managePgDatabase / queryPgDatabase) for new environments.

action.description: destroyMySQL=destroy MySQL instance; runStatement=execute write SQL or DDL; initializeSchema=run ordered schema initialization statements

request.description: Official request payload used by action=destroyMySQL

statements.description: Ordered schema initialization SQL statements used by action=initializeSchema

requireReady.description: Whether initializeSchema should block until MySQL is confirmed ready. Defaults to true.

statusContext.description: Optional instance status requests used to confirm readiness before initializeSchema (for tasks started in the console)

dbInstance.description: Optional SQL database instance context for runStatement/initializeSchema

tools.name: queryFunctions
tools.description:
Unified read-only entry for CloudBase cloud functions: function lists and details, execution logs, layers, triggers, code download URLs, published versions and traffic aliases, async deployment status, and code-package upload URLs.

**Cloud function logs**: `listFunctionLogs` queries execution logs for one function and defaults to the last day without startTime/endTime; the span must not exceed 1 day and a single call returns at most 100 entries
- `hasMore=true` means older logs exist: pass the returned `context` back unchanged to fetch the next page (`offset` only works within the first 100 entries)
- Each `logs[]` item is parsed into requestId / log / statusCode / retCode / durationMs / memoryMb / timestamp
- For the full sequence of one invocation (START, business logs, REPORT) use `getFunctionLogDetail`
- This tool queries execution logs of a specific function; for cross-service CLS log search use `queryLogs`

**Scheduled tasks / cron / timers**: use `listFunctionTriggers` to query a function's timer trigger configuration.

**Async deployment status**: `getFunctionDeployStatus` returns data.build, data.deploy, and data.progress. While status=running, data.result and data.error are null and deployment must not be reported as complete. Keep polling until status=succeeded/failed. status=expired means the task exceeded the 2-hour retention limit; cloud deployment may still be running, so confirm with getFunctionDetail. Tasks exist only in MCP process memory and are isolated by environment; expired tasks or a restarted MCP Server return errorCode=DEPLOY_TASK_NOT_FOUND. This action is unavailable in cloud mode because real cloud/local builds cannot run there, while image deployment is synchronous and creates no taskId.

**Code package upload**: `getFunctionUploadUrl` returns a COS presigned upload URL (two-phase ZIP deployment phase A): PUT the code zip to uploadUrl (include the corresponding request headers when uploadHeaders is non-empty), then call manageFunctions createFunction/updateFunctionCode with the code triplet (phase B). The uploadUrl carries credential-bound signatures; never log or persist it; it is only usable in the environment it was minted for and is valid for 300 seconds by default.

**Layers** are account-level shared namespaces in SCF; `listLayers` / `listLayerVersions` / `getLayerVersionDetail` return the account-level view, which may include layers created by other environments.
- When creating a layer, use a unique name with the environment suffix, in the fixed format `{layerName}_{current envId}` (e.g. `common_cloud1-d9ghadgak3edf6b36`). Do not reuse the same bare layer name across environments; check with `listLayers` before creating

action.description: Read-only action type. Note the layer version list is `listLayerVersions` (plural Versions); see the tool description for each action's usage and limits and the parameter descriptions for what each needs.

functionName.description: CloudBase cloud function name. Required for `getFunctionDetail`, `listFunctionLogs`, `listFunctionLayers`, `listFunctionTriggers`, `getFunctionDownloadUrl`, `listVersionByFunction`, and `getFunctionAlias`. Optional for `getFunctionUploadUrl` (only used to generate the upload object key).

limit.description: Page size (limit). Optional for list actions; the backend determines the default. Log actions return at most 100 entries and default to 20.

offset.description: Pagination offset. Optional for list actions; defaults to 0. For log actions it only works within the first 100 entries — use the returned context to page further back.

codeSecret.description: Code protection secret used to decrypt function code.

revealEnvValues.description: Whether `getFunctionDetail` / `listFunctionTriggers` / `listFunctionLayers` returns plaintext environment variable values. Defaults to false: Value is masked as ***, while Key and ValueLength remain, which is sufficient to verify configured variables and changes. true returns plaintext and may expose secrets to the model context; use cautiously. Prefer the console or CLI for plaintext values.

startTime.description: Log query start time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss format (for example, 2024-01-01 00:00:00, interpreted as Beijing time). The interval to endTime must not exceed one day. Defaults to the most recent day when omitted.

endTime.description: Log query end time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss format (for example, 2024-01-01 23:59:59, interpreted as Beijing time). The interval from startTime must not exceed one day. Defaults to the current time when omitted.

requestId.description: Log request ID. Required for `getFunctionLogDetail`; take it from logs[].requestId returned by `listFunctionLogs`, or use the RequestId printed in a business log line.

qualifier.description: Function version alias, such as $LATEST or $DEFAULT. Optional for log queries; used as a CLS filter.

context.description: Log pagination cursor. Pass the `context` returned by the previous `listFunctionLogs` call back unchanged to fetch the next page; never construct it yourself. null means there are no more results.

runtime.description: Runtime filter for layer queries, such as Nodejs18.15.

layerName.description: Layer name. Required for `listLayerVersions` and `getLayerVersionDetail`. Layers use an account-level shared namespace; use the fixed format `{layerName}_{current envId}` (for example, common_cloud1-d9ghadgak3edf6b36).

taskId.description: Async deployment task ID for `getFunctionDeployStatus` (returned by manageFunctions with wait=false). Tasks exist only in current MCP process memory: terminal tasks are retained for about 30 minutes and running tasks for at most 2 hours.

order.description: Sort direction for `listVersionByFunction`; only ASC / DESC are supported.

orderBy.description: Sort field for `listVersionByFunction`; only AddTime / ModTime are supported.

tools.name: manageFunctions
tools.description:
Unified write entry for CloudBase cloud functions. Supports creating functions, updating code, updating configuration, invoking functions, publishing versions, configuring traffic aliases, and managing timer triggers (scheduled jobs / cron) and layer bindings. The deployment package has a hard size ceiling — do not bundle static content: media files (video, large images, fonts), user uploads, and frequently-updated static resources belong in cloud storage referenced by URL, otherwise every change forces a full function redeploy and the package can exceed the limit. To create a cron scheduled task, first create the function with createFunction, then create the timer trigger with createFunctionTrigger, and delete triggers with deleteFunctionTrigger. Publish versions with `publishVersion`; shift traffic (canary) with `updateFunctionAliasConfig`. HTTP function image deployment: createFunction / updateFunctionCode choose the path via func.buildStrategy (image = deploy an existing image, local / cloud = build then deploy, omitted or zip = traditional code package). local / cloud only produce a dry-run plan by default; pass dryRun=false with confirm=true to execute the real deployment. A real deployment may pass wait=false to return a taskId immediately; query progress and results via getFunctionDeployStatus of queryFunctions. wait=false only means this tool call does not wait for the full deployment; the caller must not finish while status=running and must keep polling until succeeded/failed before reporting to the user, unless the polling limit is reached. local always requires local MCP mode; the real execution of cloud also requires local MCP mode because it reads the local build context; cloud mode only supports cloud dry-run and the image strategy. Dangerous operations require explicit confirm=true.

**Personal-edition TCR credentials**: local/cloud builds with imageType=personal need push credentials. If TCB_TCR_USERNAME and TCB_TCR_PASSWORD are set in the env of the MCP configuration, leave registryCredential empty and it is read automatically. Do not ask users for plaintext passwords, and do not put passwords into tool parameters.
Note this env channel only works with **local stdio MCP and clients whose mcp.json supports a custom env block**: some GUI clients do not inherit shell exports, and IDE built-in MCPs usually inject credentials through a hardcoded whitelist (e.g. only TENCENTCLOUD_*), so those users have no channel to configure a custom env. For built-in MCP users, guide them instead to use the enterprise edition (imageType=enterprise, instance temporary tokens, no fixed password) or to use buildStrategy=image to deploy an already-pushed image.
**Enterprise-edition login requirements**: cloud/local builds for enterprise require minting a TCR temporary token via CAM. Environment-level API keys and temporary credentials from OAuth carry no CAM policy and will be blocked up front with a hint to switch to account-level keys or the image strategy; personal edition logs in directly with a static password via docker login without CAM, and is the only build path that works for API-key users.

**Layers** are account-level shared namespaces in SCF: same-named layers created in different environments share one version sequence, and deleting a version affects every environment bound to it. When creating a layer, use a unique name with the environment suffix, in the fixed format `{layerName}_{current envId}` (e.g. `common_cloud1-d9ghadgak3edf6b36`). Do not reuse the same bare layer name across environments; check with `listLayers` before creating. Read-only queries: listLayers / listLayerVersions / getLayerVersionDetail of queryFunctions.

action.description: Write action type. createFunctionTrigger / deleteFunctionTrigger manage scheduled tasks (cron / timer); publishVersion publishes a new version; updateFunctionAliasConfig updates alias / traffic routing; incrementalDeployFunction uploads a single changed file.

func.description: Function configuration for createFunction / updateFunctionCode. Image/build deployment is selected by func.buildStrategy (zip/cloud/local/image), with image fields under func.imageConfig.

protocolType.description: HTTP function access protocol. Currently only WebSockets is supported; use WS together with protocolParams.wsParams. Do not pass this field for ordinary HTTP functions. Other values such as HTTP cause InvalidParameterValue.ProtocolType.

envVariables.description: Environment variables. If they include traditional TCP database variables such as DATABASE_URL, MYSQL_*, POSTGRES_*, or REDIS_*, also configure vpc (vpcId + subnetId), using IDs from the actual database/network configuration. Never guess them. Native app.rdb()/app.database() access does not require a VPC.

vpc.description: Private network configuration (egress). Required when using a non-native SDK to access MySQL, PostgreSQL, or Redis over TCP in a VPC. vpcId/subnetId must match the private database endpoint VPC. If unknown, check the console or ask the user; never use placeholders.

vpcId.description: VPC ID from the real database/network console (e.g. vpc-xxxxxxxx). Required for non-native TCP DB access. Do NOT invent or use placeholders.

subnetId.description: Subnet ID in the same VPC as the private DB endpoint (e.g. subnet-xxxxxxxx). Do NOT invent or use placeholders.

runtime.description:
Runtime environment. Event functions support multiple runtimes:
  Nodejs: Nodejs22.21, Nodejs20.19, Nodejs18.15, Nodejs16.13, Nodejs14.18, Nodejs12.16, Nodejs10.15, Nodejs8.9
  Python: Python3.10, Python3.9, Python3.7, Python3.6, Python2.7
  Php: Php8.0, Php7.4, Php7.2
  Java: Java8, Java11
  Golang: Golang1

Recommended runtimes:
  Node.js: Nodejs18.15
  Python: Python3.9
  PHP: Php7.4
  Java: Java11
  Go: Golang1

For image deployment (creating a function from a TCR image), use "CustomImage" and provide imageConfig; functionRootPath/zipFile is not needed.

buildStrategy.description: HTTP function deployment strategy: zip=code package deployment (default); image=use an existing image (imageConfig.imageUri required); cloud=cloud image build; local=local Docker image build. cloud/local use image build deployment orchestration and require imageConfig. build itself is optional because repository coordinates (namespace defaults to envId and repository defaults to the function name) can be filled automatically. Provide build only for build details or fields such as build.registryCredential for a personal registry.

imageConfig.description: Image configuration used with buildStrategy=image/cloud/local or runtime=CustomImage. All image fields are under this namespace. For image, set imageUri to use an existing image. For cloud/local, build may describe how to build; if omitted, default repository coordinates are filled automatically. Providing an existing image (imageUri) selects image deployment, so local code, scf_bootstrap, and Handler do not need to be packaged.

imageType.description: Image registry type: enterprise=Enterprise TCR, personal=Personal CCR. If omitted, the SDK infers enterprise when registryId is present and personal otherwise.

registryId.description: Enterprise TCR instance ID, such as tcr-xxxxxxxx. Required when imageType=enterprise; omit for personal images.

imagePort.description: HTTP image function listening port. The SDK only permits 9000; omit to use that value and do not specify another port.

entryPoint.description: Override the image entry point (ENTRYPOINT); normally unnecessary.

command.description: Override the image startup command, such as python. Omit to use the Dockerfile default.

args.description: Override image startup arguments, space-separated, such as -u app.py.

commandList.description: Array form of the image startup command, split into arguments; useful when the command itself contains spaces.

argsList.description: Array form of image startup arguments, already split; useful when an argument itself contains spaces.

containerImageAccelerate.description: Whether to enable image acceleration; recommended for large images to reduce cold-start time.

imageUri.description: Full image URL (tag required), in the format {domain}/{namespace}/{image}:{tag}, for example ccr.ccs.tencentyun.com/your-ns/demo-app:demo-app-001. Do not use :latest. Required when buildStrategy=image (existing image); optional for buildStrategy=cloud/local because the build process produces and returns the image URL. The target repository is determined by build.repository/build.namespace; explicit values take precedence. If omitted, manager-node fills defaults and creates or reuses the repository (namespace defaults to envId and repository defaults to the function name).

build.description: Image build target. Used when buildStrategy=cloud (cloud build) or local (local Docker build); omit for buildStrategy=image (existing image). build is optional for cloud/local because missing repository coordinates can be filled automatically (namespace defaults to envId and repository defaults to the function name). Provide it only to specify build details or fields such as build.registryCredential for personal registries.

cwd.description: Absolute directory for the image build context.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile path relative to build.cwd; defaults to Dockerfile.

registryId.description: Enterprise TCR instance ID; omit for personal image builds.

namespace.description: Target image namespace; defaults to current environment ID (envId).

repository.description: Target repository path without tag/digest; defaults to the function name. local personal requires the full registry/namespace/repository.

tag.description: Target image tag for local strategy; cloud generates it, so omit for cloud.

platform.description: Target image platform; currently only linux/amd64 is supported.

buildArgs.description: Docker build arguments. Do not pass secrets or credentials.

registryCredential.description: Personal TCR push credentials required by personal local/cloud builds. Prefer omitting the whole object and setting TCB_TCR_USERNAME and TCB_TCR_PASSWORD in the MCP configuration env, just like TENCENTCLOUD_SECRETID and other secrets. When environment variables are set, credentials do not need to be passed in request parameters. Explicit fields take precedence; missing fields fall back to environment variables.

username.description: Personal CCR login username, which must be the Tencent Cloud account UIN. If omitted, reads TCB_TCR_USERNAME from the MCP process environment.

password.description: Personal CCR fixed password. **Do not put a plaintext password in this field**. Set TCB_TCR_PASSWORD in the MCP configuration env and leave this field empty for automatic loading. This is sensitive and must not be logged or returned.

forceBuild.description: Whether to ignore same-digest reuse and force a rebuild.

retainedTags.description: Number of most recent image tags retained after a Personal TCR build.

localFallback.description: How to handle an unavailable local build when buildStrategy=local. Defaults to error.

config.description: Trigger configuration. timer must use the CloudBase 7-field cron format: second minute hour day month weekday year. The standard 5-field cron format is not supported (for example, */5 * * * * is invalid). Valid examples: 0 */5 * * * * * (every 5 minutes), 0 0 2 1 * * * (02:00 on the first day of every month), and 0 30 9 * * * * (09:30 every day).

isWaitInstall.description: Whether to wait for dependency installation

functionRootPath.description: Recommended local-directory input for creating or updating function code. Pass the absolute directory that directly contains function folders (e.g. /abs/path/cloudfunctions, containing <functionName>/index.js), not the project root or the function subdirectory. The SDK appends the function subdirectory; do not precompress ZIP or base64 content.

force.description: Whether createFunction overwrites an existing function.

functionName.description: Target function name at the top level. Used by updateFunctionCode, updateFunctionConfig, invokeFunction, publishVersion, updateFunctionAliasConfig, and similar actions. createFunction uses func.name; other actions use top-level functionName. A mistakenly supplied func.name is also recognized as functionName.

zipFile.description: Compatibility only: base64-encoded prebuilt code package. For ordinary createFunction/updateFunctionCode, do not create a ZIP first; prefer functionRootPath.

code.description: Two-phase ZIP deployment phase B: the code package has been uploaded to the environment COS bucket via queryFunctions action=getFunctionUploadUrl. Pass the triplet (cosBucketName/cosObjectName/cosBucketRegion) through unchanged from the getFunctionUploadUrl response. With code provided, createFunction/updateFunctionCode no longer reads local directories (functionRootPath/zipFile are unnecessary), and cloud dependency installation is skipped by default (override with func.installDependency). The triplet's bucket and region must be this environment's own bucket, and the object key must have the fnzip-upload/... form returned by getFunctionUploadUrl; hand-built triplets, a bucket from another environment, or cross-environment reuse are rejected and require fetching a new address.

cosBucketName.description: Environment bucket short name (without the -appid suffix); pass through the cosBucketName returned by getFunctionUploadUrl, do not invent one

cosObjectName.description: Uploaded object key; pass through the cosObjectName returned by getFunctionUploadUrl

cosBucketRegion.description: Bucket region; defaults to the current environment bucket region when omitted

envVariables.description: Environment variables to merge during a configuration update. If they contain TCP database variables such as DATABASE_URL, MYSQL_*, POSTGRES_*, or REDIS_*, also provide a real vpc (or ensure the function already has a complete VPC binding). Never guess vpcId/subnetId.

vpc.description: VPC information for configuration updates. Real vpcId + subnetId are required for non-native TCP database access; do not use placeholders.

vpcId.description: VPC ID from the real database/network console (e.g. vpc-xxxxxxxx). Required for non-native TCP DB access. Do NOT invent or use placeholders.

subnetId.description: Subnet ID in the same VPC as the private DB endpoint (e.g. subnet-xxxxxxxx). Do NOT invent or use placeholders.

triggers.description: Trigger list for createFunctionTrigger, used for scheduled jobs. timer triggers use a 7-field cron expression (second minute hour day month weekday year), such as "0 */5 * * * * *" for every 5 minutes.

config.description: Trigger configuration. timer must use the CloudBase 7-field cron format: second minute hour day month weekday year. The standard 5-field cron format is not supported (for example, */5 * * * * is invalid). Valid examples: 0 */5 * * * * * (every 5 minutes), 0 0 2 1 * * * (02:00 on the first day of every month), and 0 30 9 * * * * (09:30 every day).

replaceAll.description: Default false: if the function has timer triggers not listed in triggers, the tool refuses and lists their names. Set true to replace all timer triggers with this submission.

layerName.description: Layer name. When creating a layer, use `{layerName}_{current envId}` (for example, common_cloud1-d9ghadgak3edf6b36). Do not reuse a bare layer name across environments; layers use an account-level shared namespace.

contentPath.description: Only for createLayerVersion: path to layer content, either a directory or a ZIP file. To update function code, use functionRootPath / zipFile / code instead.

description.description: Description. Layer version description for createLayerVersion; version or alias description for publishVersion / updateFunctionAliasConfig.

layers.description: Target layer list for updateFunctionLayers; array order becomes final order.

codeSecret.description: Code protection secret used when binding a layer.

dryRun.description: Whether image build deployment (func.buildStrategy=cloud/local) only generates a deployment plan. Defaults to true; false also requires confirm=true.

wait.description: Whether a real image deployment waits for completion; false returns a taskId immediately and continues in the background. Defaults to true, but synchronous waiting can take about 15 minutes and hit the MCP Client timeout without a taskId to track, so pass wait=false explicitly for a real build deployment (buildStrategy=cloud/local, dryRun=false).

autoGrant.description: Whether manager-node may automatically add the fixed allowlist of CAM policies for image deployment. Defaults to false; set true only after explicitly confirming permission changes.

confirm.description: Dangerous-operation confirmation. deleteFunction, deleteFunctionTrigger, deleteLayerVersion, detachLayer, other delete actions, and real image build deployment (func.buildStrategy=cloud/local) require confirm=true.

incrementalFile.description: Changed-file path for incrementalDeployFunction incremental deployment.

functionVersion.description: Primary version for `updateFunctionAliasConfig`. May be a concrete version number or `$LATEST`.

routingConfig.description: Traffic routing config for `updateFunctionAliasConfig`. AdditionalVersionWeights is used for canary weights; AddtionVersionMatchs keeps the SCF/SDK historical field name (including the typo).

Weight.description: Additional traffic weight (0-1 or percentage per SCF convention)

AddtionVersionMatchs.description: Additional version match rules (field name keeps SCF AddtionVersionMatchs)

Version.description: Version targeted by a match rule

Key.description: Header/Query key for a match rule

Method.description: Match method, such as Exact / Regex

tools.name: queryHosting
tools.description: Read-only information about CloudBase static hosting. Lets the AI discover state first and then decide the next step: action=websiteConfig queries the index/error document, routing rules, and site domain info; action=status queries the hosting service status; action=findFiles finds files by prefix; action=listFiles lists all hosted files; action=domainStatus queries the current status and configuration of custom domains. This tool has no side effects.

action.description: Query type: websiteConfig=query the static hosting website document config and site domain info, status=query the static hosting service status, findFiles=find hosted files by prefix, listFiles=list all files in static hosting, domainStatus=query custom domain config and effective status. This tool is strictly read-only and never modifies resources.

prefix.description: File prefix filter, e.g. app/ or assets/logo. Recommended for action=findFiles to narrow the result; omitting it does not fail — it returns the first N files of the whole site so you can pick a real prefix.

marker.description: Pagination start marker. Used only with action=findFiles to continue after the previous page.

maxKeys.description: Maximum number of files returned per call. Used only with action=findFiles.

domains.description: Custom domains to query. Used only with action=domainStatus, e.g. ["www.example.com"].

tools.name: manageHosting
tools.description: Mutation operations for CloudBase static hosting. action=upload uploads local build artifacts to the shared domain (domain format: <envId>-<appId>.tcloudbaseapp.com/<cloudPath>); action=delete deletes hosted files or directories (confirm=true required); action=setWebsiteDocument sets the index/error document and routing rules; action=enableService enables static hosting; action=bindDomain / unbindDomain / updateDomain manage custom domains; action=downloadFile / downloadDirectory download hosted content to local disk. ⚠️ Every hosting operation calls the DescribeStaticStore control-plane API underneath (20 req/s QPS limit): when deleting multiple files, call sequentially with intervals (no more than 10 calls per second recommended); for multiple files in the same directory, prefer isDir=true to delete the whole directory in one call. If the error contains "frequency limit", rate limiting was triggered — wait 1-2 seconds and retry; do not retry in rapid succession. ⚠️ This tool has no action to disable the default domain (*.tcloudbaseapp.com); to disable that default public domain, use manageGateway(action="disableRoute", domain=the STATIC_STORE IsDefault domain, path="/") (backed by ModifyHTTPServiceRoute, not ModifyGatewayRoute). ⚠️ For new projects prefer manageApps (deploys to a dedicated subdomain); this tool suits existing legacy projects or as a fallback for manageApps. manageApps and manageHosting use different domains, so switching invalidates old links. If the task is only inspecting config, files, or domain status, use queryHosting instead.

action.description: Management type: upload=upload local build artifacts to static hosting, delete=delete hosted files or directories, setWebsiteDocument=set the index/error document and routing rules, enableService=enable the static hosting service, bindDomain=bind a custom domain, unbindDomain=unbind a custom domain, updateDomain=update domain cache/hotlink protection/IP rules, downloadFile=download a single hosted file locally, downloadDirectory=download a hosted directory locally.

localPath.description: Local path. With action=upload it is the local file/directory to upload; with action=downloadFile or downloadDirectory it is the local download target. An absolute path is recommended.

cloudPath.description: Target path in static hosting. With action=upload it is the hosted path after upload; with action=delete/downloadFile/downloadDirectory it is the hosted file or directory path.

files.description: Multi-file upload config. Optional and only for action=upload; when provided, files are uploaded one by one and the single localPath/cloudPath is no longer used.

localPath.description: Absolute local path of a single file to upload.

cloudPath.description: Hosted path of this file after it is uploaded to static hosting.

ignore.description: File patterns to ignore during upload. Optional and only for action=upload, e.g. node_modules or ["**/*.map", "**/.DS_Store"].

tools.name: queryStorage
tools.description:
⚠️ For PG-mode environments use queryPgStorage instead of this tool (pgstore and the legacy COS are two separate systems).

Query CloudBase cloud storage info: list directory files, get file details, get temporary download URLs, and other read-only operations. Returned file info includes name, size, modification time, download URL, etc. Note: the temporaryUrl returned by action=url is a temporary signed link whose validity is determined by the maxAge parameter (default 1 hour); do not treat it as a permanent public URL. The tool also derives publicUrl from the Storages[0].CdnDomain returned by DescribeEnvs. ⚠️ Warning: publicUrl is anonymously accessible only when the bucket ACL is public-read; with the default private-read-write bucket the returned publicUrl will 403 — keep using temporaryUrl, or first set the target path to public-read via the console/SDK.

💡 For bucket ACL permission management use the permissions tool: query with queryPermissions(action="getResourcePermission", resourceType="storage", resourceId="bucket-name"), set with managePermissions(action="updateResourcePermission", resourceType="storage", resourceId="bucket-name", permission="READONLY").

📦 CloudBase PG / pgstore environments: buckets listed in `DescribeEnvs.Storages[]` belong to the legacy NoSQL backend and are not pgstore buckets. Use this tool for regular storage; when preparing a bucket for PG browser uploads, confirm the target bucket is usable by the pgstore backend, otherwise the browser `app.storage.from().upload(...)` will fail with `STORAGE_BUCKET_NOT_FOUND` and a `PUT https://undefined/` request.

action.description: Query operation: list=list all files in a directory, info=get details for a specified file, url=get a temporary file download URL, read=read text file content

cloudPath.description: Cloud file path, for example files/data.txt or files/ (directory)

maxAge.description: Temporary URL validity in seconds, range: 1-86400, default: 3600 (1 hour)

tools.name: manageStorage
tools.description:
⚠️ For PG-mode environments use queryPgStorage instead of this tool (pgstore and the legacy COS are two separate systems).

Manage CloudBase cloud storage files — for COS/Storage objects only, not for static website hosting. Supports uploading/downloading/deleting files and directories. Delete operations require force=true as confirmation to prevent accidental deletion. Note: the temporaryUrl returned after upload is a temporary signed link that expires in 1 hour; do not write it into configuration or persistent storage as a permanent public URL. The tool also derives publicUrl from the Storages[0].CdnDomain returned by DescribeEnvs. ⚠️ Warning: publicUrl is anonymously accessible only when the bucket ACL is public-read; with the default private-read-write bucket the returned publicUrl will 403 — keep using temporaryUrl, or first set the target path to public-read via the console/SDK.

💡 For bucket ACL permission management use the permissions tool: query with queryPermissions(action="getResourcePermission", resourceType="storage", resourceId="bucket-name"), set with managePermissions(action="updateResourcePermission", resourceType="storage", resourceId="bucket-name", permission="READONLY").

📦 CloudBase PG / pgstore buckets must be created before use (same as Supabase Storage: the bucket must exist before upload). The browser SDK `app.storage.from().upload(path, file)` does not create buckets automatically, and the first segment of `path` is the bucket name (e.g. `covers/foo.png` → bucket=`covers`); the argument of `from('covers')` is currently not prepended to the path. If the browser sees `STORAGE_BUCKET_NOT_FOUND` or `PUT https://undefined/` during upload (shown as `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED` in DevTools), first confirm / create the corresponding pgstore bucket with this tool or the console, then have the frontend retry the upload — do not let the frontend silently swallow the upload failure. Legacy NoSQL buckets returned by `DescribeEnvs.Storages[]` (shaped like `<hash>-<envId>-<appId>`) are not usable pgstore buckets; never use them as the default target.

action.description: Management operation: upload=upload a file or directory, download=download a file or directory, delete=delete a file or directory

localPath.description: Local file path; an absolute path such as /tmp/files/data.txt is recommended. Required for upload/download and not needed for delete

cloudPath.description: Cloud file path, for example files/data.txt

force.description: Force-operation switch. Set to true to confirm deletion; defaults to false

isDirectory.description: Whether the operation targets a directory: true=directory, false=file; defaults to false

Supported IDE types:

- github-copilot: GitHub Copilot
