tools.name: searchKnowledgeBase
tools.description:
CloudBase knowledge base search tool. Supports CloudBase official docs (docs), fixed skill docs (skill), and OpenAPI docs (openapi).

Choose mode by scenario:
- A tool call failed with an error code in the message (e.g. OperationDenied.FreePackageDenied): mode=docs + action=searchDocs (query=error code). Look up the official meaning and guidance of the error code before acting; do not retry on guesses.
- Unsure where the answer is and need a full-text search over official docs: mode=docs + action=searchDocs
- You know the doc title, hierarchical path, or URL: mode=docs + action=findByName or action=readDoc
- Need a hands-on guide / best practices for a scenario: mode=skill + skillName
- Need an HTTP API definition: mode=openapi + apiName

⚠️ Important: when CloudBase skills are disabled or the current IDE does not support reading skill files, use searchKnowledgeBase(mode=skill, skillName=...) to get CloudBase skill doc content instead of trying to read skill files directly. Direct reads may return 400 errors. Examples: searchKnowledgeBase(mode=skill, skillName=minimal-web-baas-demo) for a minimal Web+database demo; skillName=auth-tool-cloudbase for login provider setup; skillName=auth-web-cloudbase for Web frontend login; skillName=cloudbase-agent for agent development; skillName=cloudbase-mcp for MCP connection modes (local / remote), calling tools from the shell with mcporter, or the site / plugin switches.

A skill response contains the full SKILL.md plus the URLs of all its .md files in the remote aggregate repo (CNB raw), fetchable over HTTP; relative links are rewritten to absolute URLs, and when the skill is absent from the remote repo only the inline content is returned and that is stated explicitly.

When unsure which one to pick: call with mode=skill and no skillName, or mode=openapi and no apiName, to get the current catalog with each entry's scenario / summary (currently 32 skills, 8 APIs), then call again with the name.

Note: OpenAPI doc (openapi) queries only need mode="openapi" and apiName; do not pass action — action is only for mode="docs".

skillName.description: Required for mode=skill. The skill name.

apiName.description: Required for mode=openapi. The API name.

action.description: Only for mode=docs; do not pass action with mode=openapi. CloudBase documentation action: listModules lists all documentation modules; listModuleDocs gets the catalog for a module; findByName searches intelligently by name, path, or URL; readDoc reads document Markdown; searchDocs performs a full-text search of the official documentation.

moduleName.description: Required when mode=docs and action=listModuleDocs. The module name.

input.description: Required when mode=docs and action=findByName. Accepts a module name, document title, hierarchical path, or URL.

docPath.description: Required when mode=docs and action=readDoc. A site-relative path such as /quick-start, or a document address returned by action=findByName / action=searchDocs — only the path is used; any host is ignored.

query.description: Required when mode=docs and action=searchDocs. Full-text search keywords.

tools.name: queryCloudRun
tools.description: Query CloudRun service info: list services, get service details, list available templates, get build logs (getDeployLog, cloud source builds only / depends on CODING), get runtime logs (getProcessLog, works for both image and source deploys / no CODING needed), get deploy records, and check the env's CloudRun provisioning status (envStatus). Returned info includes service name, status, access type, config details, and latest deploy context.

action.description: Query action: list=list CloudRun services (supports pagination and filtering), detail=query details of a service (including service config and latest deploy status), templates=list available project templates (for initializing new projects), getDeployLog=get build logs (only meaningful for cloud source builds, backed by CODING/DescribeCloudRunBuildLog; existing-image deploys have no build phase; accounts not logged into CODING get an error), getProcessLog=get runtime logs (deploy-phase steps plus container startup/runtime logs, backed by tcbr/DescribeCloudRunProcessLog; works for both image deploys and source builds and does not depend on CODING; RunId comes from latestDeploy.RunId of detail/getDeployRecords), getDeployRecords=list deploy records of a service (newest first, including BuildId/RunId/FlowRatio/Status, useful for release history and rollback context), envStatus=check whether CloudRun is provisioned for the current env and its status (Status=creating provisioning/normal provisioned), used to poll progress after initEnv or to confirm readiness before deploy, getManageTask=query the deploy task of a service (backed by tcbr/DescribeServerManageTask); returns the task Id/Status plus the latest deploy record status, used to tell whether a deploy is progressing or stuck (e.g. a version stuck in 'creating'). Use it to confirm the real task state when you hit "a deploy task is already running" instead of blindly retrying

pageSize.description: Page size, controlling how many services are returned per page. Range: 1-100, default: 10. Adjust based on network performance and display needs

pageNum.description: Page number for paginated queries. Starts at 1, default: 1. Use with pageSize to browse page by page

serverName.description: Service name filter with fuzzy matching. For example, "test" matches service names like "test-service" and "my-test-app". Leave empty to query all services

serverType.description: Service type filter: function=function-type CloudRun (Node.js only, with special development requirements and limits, suitable for simple API services), container=container service (recommended; supports any language and framework such as Java/Go/Python/PHP/.NET, suitable for most scenarios)

envId.description: Environment ID (used with action=envStatus; the currently configured env is used when omitted). Format: env-xxxxxx

detailServerName.description: Name of the service whose details, deploy records, build logs, or runtime logs you want. Recommended when action is detail, getDeployLog, getProcessLog, or getDeployRecords; it must be an existing service name. Use the list action to get available service names

buildId.description: Build ID, used only with action=getDeployLog (build logs, cloud source builds only). When omitted, the build log of the most recent deploy is returned

runId.description: Run ID (RunId), used only with action=getProcessLog. When omitted, the RunId of the service's most recent deploy record is used (the same source as latestDeploy.RunId in detail/getDeployRecords). Runtime logs are available for both image deploys and source builds

revealEnvParams.description: Whether to return plaintext service environment variables (ServerConfig.EnvParams) (effective only with action=detail). Default false, values are masked as "***" (keys are kept, which is enough to check which variables are configured and whether a change took effect); when true, plaintext is returned and sensitive variables (such as a DATABASE_URL containing a password) may be exposed to the model context — use with care

tools.name: manageCloudRun
tools.description: Manage CloudRun services, in development order: provision the CloudRun env (initEnv), initialize a project (optionally from a template; list templates via queryCloudRun), download service code, run locally (function services only), deploy code, update config only (updateConfig, no code upload needed), and delete the service. deploy supports two modes: 1) source build (pass targetPath; local code is packaged and uploaded, the default); 2) existing image deploy (pass imageUrl, e.g. ccr.ccs.tencentyun.com/ns/img:v1; DeployType=image container deploy, targetPath optional). deploy means "trigger deploy + lightweight wait for task registration" (up to ~45s; pass waitRegistration=false to skip the wait when you don't need the buildId). Source builds return buildId — poll getDeployLog for build progress, then getProcessLog; image deploys (imageUrl) usually have BuildId=0 — getDeployLog is skipped, and runId/next_step guide you to getProcessLog (or getDeployRecords first for RunId). If the user explicitly specifies an image or no rebuild is needed, you must pass imageUrl instead of falling back to a source build just because a local source directory exists. For existing services, deploy reads the remote config first and merges (preserving VpcConf/EnvParams/OpenAccessTypes). Deletion requires confirmation; set force=true. If a new env reports CloudRun not provisioned before the first deploy, call initEnv first (async, idempotent). Before deploying, make sure the image carries no static content: media files (video, large images, fonts), user uploads, and frequently-updated static resources belong in cloud storage referenced by URL, not in the image. Otherwise every deploy re-pushes the whole image and every scale-up instance re-pulls it — one demo video can turn a 30-second deploy into minutes.

action.description: CloudRun service management action: init=initialize new CloudRun project code from a template (creates a subdirectory named after serverName under targetPath), download=download an existing service's code locally, run=run a function-type CloudRun service locally (function services only), deploy=trigger the deploy and wait lightly for task registration (does not hang for the full build; poll getDeployLog for source builds, skip getDeployLog and use getProcessLog for image deploys), updateConfig=update the service config only without re-uploading code, delete=delete a CloudRun service (irreversible, requires confirmation), createAgent=create a function-type Agent, initEnv=provision CloudRun for the current env (asynchronous and idempotent; use before the first deploy in a new env), traffic=traffic management and canary release (sub-actions in trafficOp)

serverName.description: CloudRun service name, used to identify and manage the service. Naming rules: upper/lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores; must start with a letter; 3-45 characters. For init it is the subdirectory name created under targetPath; for other actions it is the target service name. The initEnv action does not need this parameter

trafficOp.description: Traffic management sub-action (used with action=traffic): set=adjust the canary traffic split (deploy the new version to canary first, then set stablePercent/canaryPercent); promote=release the canary version to full traffic and turn off canary release; rollback=stop the current canary/releasing version and return to the previous stable version

stablePercent.description: Stable version traffic percentage (used with trafficOp=set), range 0-100. It must sum to 100 with canaryPercent. For example, to send 90% of traffic to stable and 10% to canary, use stablePercent=90, canaryPercent=10

canaryPercent.description: Canary version traffic percentage (used with trafficOp=set), range 0-100. It must sum to 100 with stablePercent. For example, to send 90% of traffic to stable and 10% to canary, use stablePercent=90, canaryPercent=10

envId.description: Environment ID (used with action=initEnv; the currently configured env is used when omitted). Format: env-xxxxxx

packageType.description: CloudRun env package type (used with action=initEnv): Trial, Standard, Professional, Enterprise. Default Trial

vpcId.description: VPC network ID (optional with action=initEnv). Required when the platform refuses to create the network for you; format: vpc-xxxxxxxx. Passed through to VpcId/SubNetIds of CreateCloudRunEnv together with subnetIds. It can be omitted in most cases (the system creates the network)

subnetIds.description: Subnet ID list (optional with action=initEnv). Required when you need to specify your own VPC, e.g. ["subnet-xxxxxxxx"]. Passed through to SubNetIds of CreateCloudRunEnv together with vpcId

targetPath.description: Local code path; must be absolute. For deploy it is the code directory to deploy, for download the download target directory, and for init the parent directory of the CloudRun service. Recommended convention: the cloudrun/ directory under the project root. It must name a specific project directory: the filesystem root, the home directory itself, /Users itself, system directories (including /bin and /etc), and host-data directories such as .ssh, Library, or .config/.cloudbase are rejected. May be omitted for updateConfig and when deploying an existing image via imageUrl. Having a local source directory does not mean a source build is required; when the user specifies an image, prefer imageUrl.

imageUrl.description: Existing-image deploy (used with action=deploy): the container image address, e.g. ccr.ccs.tencentyun.com/ns/img:v1 or a public registry address; no local source directory is needed when provided. Publicly pullable anonymous images can be used directly; private/login-required images (such as ghcr.io) must first be docker pull'ed locally, then docker tag/push'ed to Tencent Cloud CCR, and the CCR address used here. When omitted, a source build is used. If the user explicitly mentions a specific image, or no code rebuild is needed, you must pass imageUrl for an image deploy instead of falling back to a source build.

envParamsReplaceAll.description: EnvParams merge strategy (deploy / updateConfig): false (default)=merge with the remote config by key (input overrides same-named keys, other remote keys are preserved); true=replace the remote EnvParams entirely with the input. Effective only when EnvParams is passed explicitly

serverConfig.description: Service config for deploy / updateConfig. Includes resource specs, access permissions, environment variables, logs, network, and more. When deploy omits it, existing services still merge and preserve the remote VpcConf/EnvParams/OpenAccessTypes; updateConfig needs at least one config field

OpenAccessTypes.description: Public access type config, controlling access permissions of the service: OA=office network access, PUBLIC=public access (default, reachable via an HTTPS domain), MINIAPP=mini program access, VPC=VPC access (reachable only within the same VPC). Multiple types can be configured

Cpu.description: CPU spec in cores. Allowed values: 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, and so on. Note: the memory spec must be twice the CPU spec (e.g. CPU=0.25 means memory=0.5, CPU=1 means memory=2). Affects service performance and billing

Mem.description: Memory spec in GB. Allowed values: 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and so on. Note: it must be twice the CPU spec. Affects service performance and billing

MinNum.description: Minimum instance count, controlling the minimum number of running instances. 0 allows scaling to zero (no cost when there are no requests); a value greater than 0 keeps that many instances running at all times (fast responses but higher cost). Setting 1 is recommended to reduce cold-start latency and improve user experience

MaxNum.description: Maximum instance count, controlling the maximum number of running instances. As traffic grows, the service scales out up to this count and rejects new requests beyond it. Set it based on your peak traffic

PolicyDetails.description: Autoscaling policy array, used to configure automatic scaling of the service. Multiple policies can be configured

PolicyType.description: Scaling type: cpu=scale on CPU utilization, mem=scale on memory utilization, cpu/mem=scale on CPU and memory utilization

PolicyThreshold.description: Scaling threshold as a percentage. For example, 60 means scaling is triggered when resource utilization reaches 60%

CustomLogs.description: Custom log config, used to configure log collection and storage policies of the service

Port.description: Service listening port. Function services are fixed at 3000 (the function framework listens on that port itself, so business code must not call app.listen); container services can customize it, and business code must listen on this port

EnvParams.description: Environment variable config as a JSON string. Used to pass configuration to the service code, e.g. '{"DATABASE_URL":"postgres://user:pass@10.x.x.x:5432/db","NODE_ENV":"production"}'. SDK v5.6.1+ automatically encrypts the passed environment variables with AES-256-CBC in transit. ⚠️ If EnvParams contains traditional TCP database variables such as DATABASE_URL / MYSQL_* / POSTGRES_* / REDIS_*, VpcConf must be configured as well, otherwise instances usually cannot reach databases inside the VPC

Dockerfile.description: Dockerfile name config, needed for container services only. Specifies the Dockerfile path used to build the container image; defaults to the Dockerfile in the project root

BuildDir.description: Build directory config, specifying the directory used to build the code. Use it when the code layout differs from the standard; defaults to the project root

InternalAccess.description: Internal access switch: open=enable internal access (callable directly through the CloudBase SDK), close=disable internal access

InternalDomain.description: Internal domain config, used to configure the internal access domain of the service. Effective only when internal access is enabled

EntryPoint.description: Dockerfile EntryPoint config, needed for container services only. Specifies the container entry program array, e.g. ["node","app.js"]

Cmd.description: Dockerfile Cmd config, needed for container services only. Specifies the container default command array, e.g. ["npm","start"]

InitialDelaySeconds.description: Initial delay of the port health check, in seconds. After deployment, the platform waits N seconds before probing the port, then probes roughly every 5s for about 30 consecutive attempts; the deploy is only marked failed after all 30 fail (a ~150s probe window) — it does not fail immediately after N seconds. Raise it to 60–120 for slow-starting applications

LogType.description: Log type config, specifying the log collection type of the service. Affects how logs are collected and stored

LogSetId.description: CLS log set ID config, specifying the CLS (Cloud Log Service) log set ID. CLS must be enabled first

LogTopicId.description: CLS log topic ID config, specifying the CLS (Cloud Log Service) log topic ID. CLS must be enabled first

LogParseType.description: Log parse type config, specifying how logs are parsed. Used to turn raw logs into structured data

Tag.description: Service tag config, used to mark the service type. For example, "function:" indicates a function-type service. The SDK generates it automatically from the config

OperationMode.description: Operation mode config, specifying the running mode of the service. Affects scheduling and resource allocation

SessionAffinity.description: Session affinity config, controlling whether session affinity is enabled. Once enabled, requests from the same client are routed to the same instance

TimerScale.description: Scheduled scaling config array, used to configure scheduled automatic scaling of the service. Multiple time windows can be configured, with daily/weekly/monthly recurrence

CycleType.description: Recurrence type: none=no recurrence, daily=daily, weekly=weekly, monthly=monthly

ReplicaNum.description: Target replica count for scheduled scaling, minimum 0 (scale to zero)

VpcConf.description: VPC network config (instance egress / private network). Used to attach CloudRun instances to a specified VPC so they can reach MySQL/PostgreSQL/Redis/CVM and other resources over the internal network. This is a different concept from OpenAccessTypes (how external callers reach this service). It is mandatory for TCP database connections. Do not guess VpcId/SubnetId; they must come from the database console, existing resource details, callCloudApi, or user confirmation. On creation it maps to the SDK vpcInfo(CreateType=2); existing services can use updateConfig or deploy (RMW preserves the remote VpcConf when it is not passed). After deploying/updating, verify ServerConfig.VpcConf with queryCloudRun detail

VpcId.description: VPC network ID, format: vpc-xxxxxxxx. It must be in the same region as the target database/Redis, and preferably the same VPC. Do not guess it or use placeholders; it must come from the database console, existing resource details, callCloudApi, or user confirmation. Configuring it at creation time is recommended; existing services can also pass it during deploy, and after deployment you must verify it took effect with queryCloudRun detail

SubnetId.description: Subnet ID, format: subnet-xxxxxxxx. CloudRun instances consume IPs from this subnet, so make sure enough IPs are available

VolumesConf.description: Volume mount config, selected by Type: COS (object storage bucket) or CFS (cloud file storage instance). The required fields differ

Type.description: Mount type: COS=object storage, CFS=cloud file storage. Different Type requires different fields

BucketName.description: COS bucket name, required when Type=COS

DstPath.description: Mount path inside the container, for example /mnt/data

Endpoint.description: COS endpoint, optional when Type=COS; defaults to the regional endpoint

SrcPath.description: Remote source path; leave empty to mount the whole bucket or instance root

ReadOnly.description: Mount as read-only; defaults to read-write

Type.description: Mount type: COS=object storage, CFS=cloud file storage. Different Type requires different fields

InstanceId.description: CFS file storage instance ID, required when Type=CFS

DstPath.description: Mount path inside the container, for example /mnt/data

MountIP.description: CFS mount IP, optional when Type=CFS

KeyID.description: CFS access key ID, optional when Type=CFS

SrcPath.description: Remote source path; leave empty to mount the whole bucket or instance root

ReadOnly.description: Mount as read-only; defaults to read-write

PublicNetStatus.description: Public access switch: ENABLE to turn public access on, DISABLE to turn it off

template.description: Project template identifier, specifying the template used when initializing a project. Use the templates action of queryCloudRun to list available templates. Common templates: helloworld=Hello World example, nodejs=Node.js project template, python=Python project template, and so on

runOptions.description: Local run parameters, supported by function-type CloudRun services only. Used to configure the local development runtime; it does not affect cloud deployments

port.description: Local run port, effective for function services only. Specifies the port the service listens on locally, default 3000. Make sure the port is not already in use

envParams.description: Extra environment variables for local runs, used for local development and debugging. Key-value pairs, e.g. {"DEBUG":"true","LOG_LEVEL":"debug"}. These variables apply to local runs only

runMode.description: Run mode: normal=plain function mode, agent=Agent mode (for AI agent development)

agentId.description: Agent ID, used in agent mode to identify a specific Agent instance

agentConfig.description: Agent config, used only with the createAgent action

agentName.description: Agent name, used to generate the BotId

botTag.description: Bot tag, used to generate the BotId; generated automatically when omitted

template.description: Agent template type, defaults to blank (empty template)

force.description: Force switch, used to skip confirmation prompts. Default false (confirmation required); true skips all confirmation steps. Setting true is strongly recommended for delete operations to avoid accidental interruptions

serverType.description: Service type: function=function-type CloudRun (Node.js only, with special development requirements and limits, suitable for simple API services), container=container service (recommended; supports any language and framework such as Java/Go/Python/PHP/.NET, suitable for most scenarios). When omitted it is detected automatically: 1) the existing service type 2) a Dockerfile exists→container 3) a @cloudbase/aiagent-framework dependency exists→function 4) otherwise→container

waitRegistration.description: Whether deploy waits for the platform to register this release (default true, up to ~45s). Waiting yields the identifier needed for follow-up queries (BuildId for source builds, RunId for image deploys). Set false to probe once and return immediately - faster, and suitable when you don't need the buildId and will query the deploy-task state on demand instead

tools.name: deployBuild
tools.description:
Parses cloudbaserc and runs a local build for every hosting[] item that declares a buildCommand (only buildCommand runs — no dependency install, no upload). It only handles hosting[] and does NOT handle the cloudbaserc app resource — app artifacts must be built by you in the project directory (read the build command and output directory from deployPlan's buildHint), or use the CLI `tcb app deploy` for a cloud build instead. Declarative hosting deployment is split into three steps — build → plan → apply — and this tool is the first one: build the artifacts locally, preview with deployPlan, then upload them with deployApply. deployApply builds neither app nor hosting — missing artifacts fail with BUILD_OUTPUT_NOT_FOUND; for hosting run this tool, for app build it yourself. Pure static hosting (no buildCommand and no detectable framework) is skipped automatically. The build is a purely local operation: it resolves no environment, requires no login and needs no confirm.
- cwd: project root, defaults to the current working directory
- mode: environment name; when it matches envOverrides.<mode> the corresponding multi-environment overrides are merged

cwd.description: Project root directory; cloudbaserc is searched below it. Defaults to the current working directory.

mode.description: Environment name, such as production/staging. Matching envOverrides.<mode> values are merged.

tools.name: deployPlan
tools.description:
Parse cloudbaserc and compute the declarative deployment plan (dry-run, makes no changes). This is the preview counterpart of deployApply: plan computes and deployApply executes the same cloudbaserc. Returns an action classification per resource: create=create new, update=overwrite update, skip=no change/will not run, conflict=conflict detected, abort, deploy=direct overwrite. The plan is recomputed by yes into the actions that will actually happen: without yes=true, functions already in the cloud are marked skip (with update kept in declaredStatus), consistent with deployApply's actual execution, avoiding a plan/execution mismatch.
⚠️ app / hosting plan items are always a direct upload of existing artifacts: declarative deploy deploys but never builds; buildCommand / framework in cloudbaserc are only used to infer the output directory and are never executed.
app / hosting plan items carry buildHint = { buildCommand, outputDir, artifactReady } (machine-readable — do not parse the localized text in details): artifactReady=false means the output directory is missing or empty, and deployApply is guaranteed to fail (BUILD_OUTPUT_NOT_FOUND). Build first, then apply — for hosting call deployBuild; for app run buildHint.buildCommand in the project directory (null means no build is needed). Re-run deployPlan afterwards to confirm artifactReady=true; do not edit the config to work around it.
Scope: this tool is for project-level declarative orchestration (one cloudbaserc for unified plan/apply); for ad-hoc single-resource direct upload use manageFunctions/manageHosting/manageApps.
- cwd: project root, defaults to the current working directory
- mode: environment name; when it matches envOverrides.<mode>, the corresponding multi-environment overrides are merged
- envId: target environment ID, takes priority over envId in cloudbaserc; if omitted, the config value or the currently bound environment is used
- only: compute the plan for the specified resource types only
- skip: skip the specified resource types
- yes: aligned with deployApply's yes, used to recompute the effective action for existing functions. true=previewed as overwrite update (update); false (default)=previewed as conservative skip (skip)

cwd.description: Project root directory; cloudbaserc is searched below it. Defaults to the current working directory.

mode.description: Environment name, such as production/staging. Matching envOverrides.<mode> values are merged.

envId.description: Target environment ID. Takes precedence over envId in cloudbaserc; when omitted, uses the config value or currently bound environment.

only.description: Compute the plan only for the specified resource types.

yes.description: Aligned with deployApply yes and used to recompute the effective action for existing functions. true previews overwrite update; false (default) previews conservative skip.

tools.name: deployApply
tools.description:
Parse cloudbaserc and execute the declarative deployment in the order database→functions→app→hosting→gateway. This is the execution counterpart of deployPlan (plan previews / deployApply executes the same cloudbaserc), a local form of apply (reads the local cloudbaserc and uploads local artifacts to the cloud). It is a write operation that changes cloud resources and requires an explicit confirm=true to execute. It is recommended to preview with deployPlan first and execute after confirming the plan.
⚠️ Deploys but never builds: this tool runs no build command at all (neither app nor hosting). buildCommand / installCommand / framework in cloudbaserc are only used to infer the output directory and are never executed. A missing or empty output directory fails with BUILD_OUTPUT_NOT_FOUND — for hosting call deployBuild first, for app ask the user to run its build command in the project directory, then retry; do not edit the config to work around it. Before building, read buildHint.buildCommand / outputDir / artifactReady from deployPlan to see what needs to run. When app needs a cloud build, use the CLI `tcb app deploy` (this tool provides no cloud build).
Scope: this tool is for project-level declarative orchestration (one cloudbaserc for unified plan/apply); for ad-hoc single-resource direct upload use manageFunctions/manageHosting/manageApps.
- confirm: must be explicitly true to execute the deployment, otherwise it is rejected
- confirmDestructive: when the pending database migrations contain destructive statements (DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE, ALTER…DROP/RENAME), besides confirm, confirmDestructive=true must also be explicitly passed to execute; otherwise it is rejected and the matched migrations and statements are listed. This parameter has no effect when there are no destructive migrations
- cwd: project root, defaults to the current working directory
- mode: environment name; when it matches envOverrides.<mode>, the corresponding multi-environment overrides are merged
- envId: target environment ID, takes priority over envId in cloudbaserc; if omitted, the config value or the currently bound environment is used
- only: deploy only the specified resource types
- skip: skip the specified resource types
- yes: how to handle existing resources. true=overwrite directly; false (default)=conservatively skip; in non-interactive scenarios existing resources will not be overwritten (same semantics as deployPlan's yes)
- concurrency: maximum parallelism for resources of the same type, default 1 (serial)
- continueOnError: continue deploying the remaining resources after one fails (a database failure still aborts)

confirm.description: Dangerous-operation confirmation. Deployment changes cloud resources and requires explicit confirm=true.

confirmDestructive.description: Destructive database change confirmation. When pending migrations contain DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE or ALTER…DROP/RENAME, explicitly pass confirmDestructive=true in addition to confirm=true. It has no effect without destructive migrations.

cwd.description: Project root directory; cloudbaserc is searched below it. Defaults to the current working directory.

mode.description: Environment name, such as production/staging. Matching envOverrides.<mode> values are merged.

envId.description: Target environment ID. Takes precedence over envId in cloudbaserc; when omitted, uses the config value or currently bound environment.

only.description: Deploy only the specified resource types.

yes.description: Whether to overwrite existing resources directly. true overwrites; false (default) conservatively skips existing resources.

concurrency.description: Maximum parallelism for resources of the same type. Defaults to 1 (serial); dependency order across resource types is unchanged.

continueOnError.description: Whether to continue deploying remaining resources after one fails; database failures always abort.

tools.name: queryGateway
tools.description: Unified read-only entry for the CloudBase HTTP gateway (Domain/Route). Query path routes under a domain and their upstreams: WEB_SCF/SCF=cloud functions, CBR=CloudRun, STATIC_STORE=static hosting, STORAGE=cloud storage, LH=Lighthouse. The primary key is Domain + Path; listRoutes / getRoute / listCustomDomains / getPrivilege / cachePurgeTask. getPrivilege queries the HTTP gateway master switch (enableService) and access auth (enableAuth) status. cachePurgeTask queries cache purge tasks for a domain (use the TaskId from manageGateway purgeCache). Before setting up custom domain access, run listCustomDomains first: if a custom domain already exists, prefer createRoute to attach a route (no certificate ID needed); use bindCustomDomain only when no usable custom domain exists.

action.description: Read-only action. getPrivilege needs no other parameter and returns the HTTP gateway master switch and access auth status directly. cachePurgeTask requires domain. For custom domain access, run listCustomDomains first to check whether an existing domain can be reused.

targetName.description: Upstream resource name filter (UpstreamResourceName): a cloud function name, CloudRun service name, or static-hosting instance name (commonly staticstore).

path.description: Route path. Optional as a getRoute / listRoutes filter

domain.description: Domain. Optional as a getRoute / listRoutes filter; required for cachePurgeTask

cacheType.description: Cache layer (cachePurgeTask only): CDN or EO. When omitted it is matched from the domain access type (EO→EO, CDN→CDN); DIRECT / CUSTOM / NONE domains have no CloudBase-hosted cache and are rejected with an explanation.

taskId.description: Cache purge task ID (cachePurgeTask only, optional filter)

purgeType.description: Purge type filter (cachePurgeTask only): PURGE_URL=by URL, PURGE_PREFIX=by path prefix, PURGE_HOST=whole domain

startTime.description: Task start time (cachePurgeTask only, optional). Format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss

endTime.description: Task end time (cachePurgeTask only, optional). Format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss

limit.description: Max records to return (cachePurgeTask only, optional)

tools.name: manageGateway
tools.description: Unified write entry for the CloudBase HTTP gateway (Domain/Route). createRoute/updateRoute/deleteRoute forward a path under a domain to an upstream; enableRoute/disableRoute enable or disable existing routes (Routes[].Enable of ModifyHTTPServiceRoute underneath, not ModifyGatewayRoute); bindCustomDomain/deleteCustomDomain manage custom domains; enableService/authSwitch toggle the HTTP gateway master switch and access auth; purgeCache clears domain cache (returns a TaskId; check progress with queryGateway cachePurgeTask). When domain is omitted, the IsDefault default HTTP domain with DomainType=HTTPSERVICE (like *.{region}.app.tcloudbase.com) is used; static-hosting CDN domains (*.tcloudbaseapp.com, DomainType=STATIC_STORE) are never used. These are path routes on the gateway default domain, not STATIC_STORE upstream bindings; a STATIC_STORE upstream must pass upstreamResourceType=STATIC_STORE explicitly. To disable the static-hosting default domain (*.tcloudbaseapp.com): first queryGateway(listRoutes) to find the domain with DomainType=STATIC_STORE and IsDefault=true, then manageGateway(action="disableRoute", domain=that domain, path="/"); do not use manageHosting. After creation, verify Domain / DomainType / Path / UpstreamResourceType via queryGateway(action="listRoutes"). The upstream type uses a single parameter upstreamResourceType (or route.upstreamResourceType, route wins), together with targetName or route.serviceName for the upstream instance. createRoute only creates the gateway entry and does not change upstream permissions. ⚠️ Custom domain access: if the env already has a custom domain (queryGateway listCustomDomains first), prefer createRoute with that domain explicitly, no certificateId needed; use bindCustomDomain only when binding a brand-new custom domain for the first time. createRoute / bindCustomDomain run VerifyHTTPServiceRoute ownership pre-checks before creation; on failure, data.checks and DNS TXT guidance are returned; configure and retry. CORS/security domains (browser cross-origin allowlist, unrelated to the gateway custom domains of this tool) use manageEnv(action=addSecurityDomain/removeSecurityDomain). If access returns HTTPSERVICE_NONACTIVATED after createRoute, the master switch is usually off (query via queryGateway getPrivilege, enable via enableService). updateRoute only needs the fields you want to change — untouched CORS/rewrite/QPS/extension settings are carried over from the live route.

action.description: Write action. createRoute/updateRoute must provide upstreamResourceType; enableRoute/disableRoute need path (passing domain explicitly is recommended) and locate the existing route first, so the upstream usually does not need to be repeated; enableService/authSwitch require enable; purgeCache requires domain and targets. Custom domain setup guide: https://docs.cloudbase.net/service/custom-domain

targetName.description: Upstream resource name (UpstreamResourceName); use either this or route.serviceName (route wins). Cloud function=function name; CloudRun=service name; static hosting=instance name (commonly staticstore). The upstream type is never inferred automatically.

path.description: Trigger path (the gateway match prefix), defaults to /{upstream name}. Examples: cloud function /api/hello, CloudRun /api, static hosting / or /app. This only creates the gateway entry; together with enablePathTransmission it determines the path the upstream actually receives.

upstreamResourceType.description: Upstream type (use either this or route.upstreamResourceType, route wins). For STORAGE, the upstream name is the cloud storage instance name — look it up with queryStorage first. Do not pass the manageFunctions type=HTTP|Event value into this field.

auth.description: Gateway path auth (EnableAuth). Usually false for anonymous/browser public access. It only controls the gateway entry; cloud function security rules, CloudRun auth, and static hosting permissions must be configured with their own tools.

enablePathTransmission.description: Path transmission (EnablePathTransmission), platform default false. With path=/api and a request to /api/users: false→the upstream receives /users; true→the upstream receives /api/users. CBR CloudRun (Express and similar self-managed sub-routes) and multi-path WEB_SCF functions often need true; STATIC_STORE mapping a trigger path to the site root (e.g. /app → hosting /) is usually false; keep false for single-entry/root-path handling. route.enablePathTransmission also works (route wins).

enableSafeDomain.description: CORS / legit-domain check (EnableSafeDomain), the console's "cross-origin settings". true validates the request origin; false skips the check (common for browser-to-API calls). route.enableSafeDomain also works (route wins).

pathRewrite.description: Path rewriting (PathRewrite), e.g. {prefix:"/v1", staticStorePrefix:"app"}. prefix replaces the matched path prefix; staticStorePrefix is the target prefix for static hosting. Omit when no rewriting is needed; route.pathRewrite also works (route wins).

qpsPolicy.description: Rate limiting (QPSPolicy), the console's "frequency limit". {total: total QPS, perClient:{limitBy:"ClientIP"|"UserID", limitValue: per-client QPS}}. Omit for no limit; route.qpsPolicy also works (route wins).

extension.description: Route-level extension: custom request/response headers and cache rules. ⚠️ The default domain (*.{region}.app.tcloudbase.com) rejects custom response headers; a custom domain is required. route.extension also works (route wins).

action.description: Write strategy: APPEND_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD=append; ADD_IF_ABSENT=add only when missing; OVERWRITE_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD=overwrite or add; OVERWRITE_IF_EXISTS=overwrite existing only

When enableRoute/disableRoute targets *.tcloudbaseapp.com, this domain must be passed explicitly. With an existing custom domain, pass it explicitly to configure routes without a certificate ID; for bindCustomDomain only, it means the new domain to bind.

certificateId.description: Certificate ID. Used only by bindCustomDomain: passing it explicitly skips the automatic search; when omitted, describeCertificates(SearchKey=domain) is called by domain — a single certificate is selected automatically, no certificate raises an error, and multiple certificates return structured selection guidance (MCP is non-interactive). createRoute / updateRoute / deleteRoute on an existing custom domain do not need certificateId.

tools.name: queryAppAuth
tools.description: Read-only entry for CloudBase app-side authentication configuration. Queries login methods, providers, publishable key, API keys, client config, and static domain to check auth readiness. ⚠️ This is a management-side config query tool; it does not perform user login. When a task asks you to write client login code (e.g. "login with the JS SDK"), first confirm the configuration via this tool, then write @cloudbase/js-sdk client login code (e.g. auth.signInWithPassword()) in the project code instead of using this tool to log in. If the app should accept plain username-style identifiers, query action=getLoginConfig first; if usernamePassword=false, immediately call manageAppAuth(action=patchLoginStrategy, patch={ usernamePassword: true }) next — do not write email login APIs directly.

providerId.description: Provider identifier, such as email or google.

clientId.description: OAuth client_id or DescribeClient Id. Defaults to the current environment ID (the default client) when omitted.

keyType.description: API key type filter. Allowed values are publish_key and api_key.

pageNumber.description: API key list page number, starting from 1.

pageSize.description: Number of API keys per page.

tools.name: manageAppAuth
tools.description: Write entry for CloudBase app-side authentication configuration. Modifies login methods, providers, and client config, ensures the publishable key, and creates or deletes API keys and custom login keys. ⚠️ This is a management-side config tool; it does not perform user login. When a task asks you to write client login code (e.g. "login with the JS SDK"), first complete the configuration here (e.g. enable usernamePassword, obtain the publishable key), then write @cloudbase/js-sdk client login code (e.g. auth.signInWithPassword()) in the project code instead of using this tool to log in. If the frontend should accept plain username-style identifiers, run action=patchLoginStrategy with patch={ usernamePassword: true } first, then implement the corresponding frontend login logic. ⚠️ Phone SMS verification code login (patch={ phone: true }) only turns the switch on: you still need to integrate your own SMS provider before any code is delivered. Prefer email verification code login to get a login flow working. See https://docs.cloudbase.net/authentication-v2/auth/custom-sms-provider for the SMS channel setup. ⚠️ The created field in the action=createApiKey response indicates whether a key was really created: created=false means an existing key in the environment was reused — the keyName/expireIn inputs take no effect, the returned keyName/expireAt are the server's real values, and warnings are attached. Never distribute it as a temporary credential.

patch.description: Simplified login strategy patch for patchLoginStrategy, such as { usernamePassword: true }.

providerId.description: Provider identifier, such as email or google. For addProvider, it can also be a custom provider Id.

displayName.description: Display name for addProvider; accepts a string or a localized object.

clientId.description: Client Id for updateClientConfig. Defaults to the current environment ID when omitted.

config.description: Configuration object for the provider or client.

keyType.description: API key type for createApiKey; defaults to publish_key.

keyName.description: API key name for createApiKey. The server may ignore this value, for example when publish_key is unique per environment. The keyName in the response always reflects the name actually stored by the server.

expireIn.description: Lifetime in seconds for createApiKey; 0 means no expiration. This value has no effect when an existing key is reused, in which case the response includes created=false and warnings.

keyId.description: Unique API key identifier for deleteApiKey.

tools.name: queryApps
tools.description:
Query CloudBase deployed apps and versions. Supports app list/detail and version list/detail; after deployment, poll build status by buildId with getAppVersion; getBuildLog retrieves build logs to diagnose failures.
action=getUploadUrl (read-only) returns a pre-signed upload URL: without a local filesystem (cloud mode), fetch the uploadUrl, PUT the code zip yourself, then call manageApps(action=deployApp, cosTimestamp) with the returned unixTimestamp to trigger deployment. The uploadUrl is a one-time upload credential; do not forward it or paste it into tickets.

serviceName.description: CloudBase app service name. Required for getApp, listAppVersions, getAppVersion, getBuildLog, and getUploadUrl. Reuse the same serviceName after redeployment to query its version history.

searchKey.description: Keyword for fuzzy matching app service names; used only when action=listApps.

versionName.description: Version name. For getAppVersion, provide either this or buildId; prefer this value when the version name is known.

buildId.description: Build ID, accepted as a number or numeric string. For getAppVersion, provide either this or versionName. A BuildId returned by deployment can be passed directly to poll status. Required for getBuildLog.

start.description: Build log offset for fetching subsequent pages. Used only when action=getBuildLog; omit it to start from the beginning.

tools.name: manageApps
tools.description:
Deploy web apps to CloudBase (builds frontend and backend, deploys to a dedicated subdomain).
Cloud upload channel (cloud mode, no local filesystem): queryApps(action=getUploadUrl) or manageApps(action=getUploadUrl) returns a pre-signed upload URL → agent PUTs the code zip to uploadUrl itself (with uploadHeaders and Content-Type: application/zip) → call deployApp with the returned unixTimestamp as cosTimestamp to trigger deployment.
action=getUploadUrl returns the pre-signed upload URL (used in cloud mode), including the upload address and cosTimestamp.
action=deployApp uploads the source ZIP and triggers the remote build & deploy pipeline:
  1. Remote npm install (skip with installCmd="")
  2. Remote npm run build (skip with buildCmd="")
  3. Remote tcb hosting deploy

Domain format: `<serviceName>-<envId>.webapps.tcloudbase.com` (one dedicated subdomain per serviceName)

✅ Recommended usage (new projects / web apps needing a dedicated domain, prefer this tool):
  For a new project's first deployment, pass framework=static, installCmd="", buildCmd="" to skip the remote build
  and only run tcb hosting deploy. After deployment you get a dedicated subdomain with version management.

⚠️ Compatibility note:
- If an existing project was previously deployed with manageHosting (domain format: `<envId>-<appId>.tcloudbaseapp.com`),
  switching to manageApps produces a brand-new URL and old links break. Keep the original deployment method.
- To check: call queryHosting to see whether hosting files already exist.

Comparison with manageHosting:
- manageApps (this tool, preferred for new projects): domain `<serviceName>-<envId>.webapps.tcloudbase.com`, dedicated subdomain, version management
- manageHosting (existing projects or fallback): domain `<envId>-<appId>.tcloudbaseapp.com/<path>`, shared environment domain
Both support custom domains.

⚠️ If the manageApps build fails, check logs with queryApps(action="getBuildLog") first; if it still fails, fall back to manageHosting.

serviceName.description: CloudBase app service name, included in the domain as `<serviceName>-<envId>.webapps.tcloudbase.com`. Reusing an existing serviceName with deployApp creates a new deployment version and triggers redeployment instead of deleting and recreating the app. Use a new name for the first deployment.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the local project root to upload and deploy. Required for deployApp in local mode. Usually this is the source directory containing package.json and source files, not the dist directory; specify the output directory with buildPath. Omit this in cloud mode and use cosTimestamp instead.

cosTimestamp.description: COS timestamp returned as unixTimestamp by getUploadUrl; accepts a string or number. When provided, creates the app from previously uploaded code and skips local packaging and upload. Obtain a pre-signed URL with getUploadUrl and PUT the ZIP first. Required in cloud mode. Exactly one of filePath and cosTimestamp must be provided.

appPath.description: Online hosting mount path for the app, for example /my-web-app. This is not a local directory path. CloudApp has a dedicated subdomain, so the default is / when omitted.

buildPath.description:
Build output directory relative to filePath, such as dist or build.
⚠️ When set, the remote build system changes to this directory before running tcb hosting deploy, so deployCmd automatically uses . (the current directory) instead of the directory name to avoid duplicated paths such as dist/dist.
It can be omitted for static HTML in the project root, but note that deployCmd defaults to dist.

framework.description: Frontend framework. Even static uses the remote build pipeline. If the app is already built locally, use manageHosting to upload it directly and skip the remote build entirely.

nodeJsVersion.description: Node.js version used for the build; when omitted, CloudBase uses its default.

installCmd.description: Dependency installation command, for example npm install. Defaults to npm install when omitted. Pass an empty string '' when dependencies are already installed or no installation is needed, though the remote pipeline still runs tcb hosting deploy.

buildCmd.description: Build command, for example npm run build. Defaults to npm run build when omitted. Pass an empty string '' to skip the build step when the app is already built locally. To skip the remote pipeline entirely, use manageHosting.

deployCmd.description: Custom deployment command. Usually unnecessary; a tcb hosting deploy command is generated automatically. When buildPath is set, the remote process has already changed to that directory and defaults to . as the source path; otherwise it defaults to dist.

ignore.description:
Glob patterns for files and directories to exclude from upload, for example **/node_modules/**.
⚠️ Packaging starts at the project root (filePath), not the buildPath output directory. Add large build outputs at the project root, such as target/ (Rust), .next/, dist-old/, or build/, to ignore (for example **/target/**), or the entire directory will be included in the upload ZIP. By default, node_modules, .git, .DS_Store, **/target/**, .next/**, and .next.bak/** are excluded.

versionName.description: Historical version name to delete; required only when action=deleteAppVersion.

tools.name: queryPermissions
tools.description:
Query CloudBase permissions and user config: resource permissions (database/functions/buckets etc.), role list/detail, app user list/detail, and gateway OPA authorization policies.

Examples:
- List legacy gateway policies: `action="listPolicy"` (an empty list only means "no policy" when the query really ran; on PG / OPA engine environments the query is skipped and returns `skipped=true` with an empty list, which does **not** mean there is no policy — use getPolicy instead)
- Read user Rego: `action="getPolicy"`; platform extension policy: `action="getPolicy", extension=true`

📌 Cross-backend boundary note: before calling, check `EnvInfo.RuntimeBackends` via `queryEnv(action="info", envId=...)`. `resourceType="noSqlDatabase"` queries CloudBase NoSQL collection rules, which are a separate mechanism from row-level security (RLS) on CloudBase PostgreSQL (PG) tables — in the same PG environment, if NoSQL collections are still in use, querying them with this tool **remains valid**. To query PG table RLS, use `queryPgDatabase(action="sql", sql="SELECT * FROM pg_policies WHERE tablename=...")` instead. This tool does not cover MySQL permissions.

⚠️ PostgreSQL environments: the platform `DescribeResourcePermission` API rejects PG environments outright. When `resourceType="function"`, this tool automatically falls back to the Manager SDK `describeEnvAuthzConfig` (aligned with CLI `tcb policy get`, reading `authz.user.rego`). For explicit OPA policies use `listPolicy` / `getPolicy`.

⚠️ Role actions (`listRoles` / `getRole`) are rejected outright by the platform on **PostgreSQL environments** (`The current API does not support PostgreSQL type environments.`). This is a platform capability boundary, not a configuration problem — **do not keep retrying on PG**; use RLS (`managePgDatabase(action="execute")` with `CREATE POLICY`) or the console to manage permissions instead.

extension.description: Used only when action=getPolicy. Set true to read the platform policy configured specifically for this environment (authz.platform.extension.rego); the default false reads the user policy (authz.user.rego). Aligned with CLI `tcb policy get --extension`.

policyResourceType.description: Used only when action=listPolicy. Filters by resource type; currently only `policy` is supported. Aligned with CLI `tcb policy list --resource-type policy`.

tools.name: managePermissions
tools.description:
Manage CloudBase permissions and user config: modify resource permissions (database/functions/buckets etc.), role management, member/policy add & remove, app user CRUD, and setting gateway OPA Rego policies.

Examples:
- Set a bucket to private: `action="updateResourcePermission", resourceType="storage", resourceId="bucket-name", permission="PRIVATE"`
- Open a cloud function to anonymous/unauthenticated access (PG goes through OPA): `action="updateResourcePermission", resourceType="function", resourceId="myFn", permission="CUSTOM", securityRule='{"invoke":true}'`
- Set user Rego directly: `action="setPolicy", regoContent="package authz.user\n\ndefault allow := false\n", confirm=true` (⚠️ immediately disables legacy gateway authorization)

Note: `createUser` / `updateUser` are environment-side app user management capabilities, suitable for test accounts, administrators, or pre-provisioned users; they should not replace the Web SDK signup form in the browser. For frontend username/password signup use `auth.signUp({ username, password })` and for login `auth.signInWithPassword({ username, password })`. Creating username/password users directly in the browser with `auth.signUp` depends on SDK/provider support and must be verified before use; if unsupported, go through a backend or management API boundary and never expose keys in the browser. The detailed semantics of `securityRule` depend on `resourceType`: `doc._openid`, `auth.openid`, query-condition subset validation, and the `create` / `update` / `delete` JSON templates only apply to document database security rules with `resourceType="noSqlDatabase"`; when configuring `function` or `storage`, refer to their official security rule docs instead of reusing NoSQL templates.

📌 Cross-backend boundary note: before calling, check `EnvInfo.RuntimeBackends` via `queryEnv(action="info", envId=...)`:
- `resourceType="noSqlDatabase"` only affects CloudBase NoSQL document database collections; row-level permissions of CloudBase PostgreSQL (PG) tables are **not** controlled by it — for PG tables use RLS instead: run `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and `CREATE POLICY ...` via `managePgDatabase(action="execute", confirm=true)`. In the same PG environment, if NoSQL collections are still in use, continuing to use `noSqlDatabase` rules for those **collections** is correct — it does not mean "this tool is disabled on PG environments".
- `resourceType="storage"` controls NoSQL/COS bucket ACLs; PG `pgstore` buckets are not covered by this `resourceType`.
- This tool does not cover MySQL; for MySQL database permissions use MySQL's own GRANT/REVOKE statements (via `manageMysqlDatabase`).

⚠️ PostgreSQL environments: the platform `ModifyResourcePermission` API rejects PG environments outright. When `resourceType="function"`, this tool automatically falls back to the Manager SDK `modifyEnvAuthzConfig` (writing `authz.user.rego`). `securityRule` accepts a full Rego document (`package authz.user`) or `'{"invoke":true}'` (auto-generates a policy allowing anonymous/unauthenticated calls to functions). Setting Rego replaces the environment-wide user policy document (it applies to the whole environment, not a single function/resource); legacy gateway authorization is disabled immediately and never rolls back, same as the CLI. Prefer `action="setPolicy"` for explicit OPA policies.

⚠️ Role actions (`createRole` / `deleteRoles` / `updateRole`) are rejected outright by the platform on **PostgreSQL environments** (`The current API does not support PostgreSQL type environments.`). This is a platform capability boundary, not a configuration problem — **do not keep retrying on PG**; use RLS (`managePgDatabase(action="execute")` with `CREATE POLICY`) or the console to manage permissions instead.

resourceType.description: Target resource type. The exact semantics of `securityRule` depend on this value. `noSqlDatabase` uses collection security rules, while `function` and `storage` each have distinct security rule semantics; do not apply NoSQL rule syntax to them.

securityRule.description: Resource-type-specific rule content whose semantics depend on `resourceType`. When `resourceType="noSqlDatabase"` and `permission="CUSTOM"`, pass document database security rules as JSON (see `https://docs.cloudbase.net/database/security-rules`); keys are typically `read`, `create`, `update`, and `delete`, with expressions as values. Important: a `create` rule validates incoming data before the document exists, so it cannot use `doc.*`; `read`, `update`, and `delete` rules may reference existing fields with `doc.*`. Do not apply `doc._openid`, `auth.openid`, query-condition subset validation, or `create` / `update` / `delete` templates to `function`, `storage`, or `sqlDatabase`. For `function` or `storage`, consult the official security rule documentation instead: functions at `https://docs.cloudbase.net/cloud-function/security-rules` and storage at `https://docs.cloudbase.net/storage/security-rules`. Example: {"read":"auth.uid != null","create":"auth.uid != null && auth.loginType != "ANONYMOUS"","update":"auth.uid != null && doc._openid == auth.openid","delete":"auth.uid != null && doc._openid == auth.openid"}

roleIdentity.description: Role identifier using letters, numbers, or _-:@. Required when action=createRole and used to reference the role programmatically.

policyIds.description: Policy ID list. Direct binding by ID is not currently supported; pass policy detail objects through policies instead.

regoContent.description: Used only when action=setPolicy. Full user OPA Rego document; it must begin with `package authz.user`. Aligned with CLI `tcb policy set <regoContent>`.

confirm.description: Used only when action=setPolicy. Setting Rego immediately disables legacy gateway authorization, so confirm=true must be passed explicitly, matching the CLI confirmation prompt.

tools.name: queryLogs
tools.description:
Unified read-only entry for the CloudBase logs domain. Supports checking log service status and searching CLS logs.

**Important distinction**:
- Query cloud function logs: use `queryFunctions(action="listFunctionLogs", functionName="xxx")`
- Query CLS logs (cross-service log aggregation): use this tool `queryLogs(action="searchLogs")`
- Enable the CLS log service: use `manageLogs(action="createLogService", confirm=true)`

**Use cases**:
- Check whether the CLS log service is enabled: `action="checkLogService"`
- Cross-service log search (e.g. find all ERROR logs): `action="searchLogs"`
- Search logs of a specific service with CLS syntax: `action="searchLogs", service="tcb|tcbr"`

action.description:
Operation type:
- `checkLogService`: Check whether the CLS log service is enabled
- `searchLogs`: Search CLS logs (requires queryString)

queryString.description:
CLS query statement. **Required when action="searchLogs"** and must strictly follow CLS (Cloud Log Service) syntax; see https://cloud.tencent.com/document/api/876/128127.

**Cloud function queries**:
- Cloud function logs: `(src:app OR src:system) AND log:"START RequestId"`
- Aggregate cloud function request status: `| select request_id, max(status_code) as status where ((request_id='44738f94-16dd-11f1-****' AND retry_num=0) AND retry_num=0) AND status_code!=202 group by request_id, retry_num`

**Document database**:
- Document database: `module:database`
- Document database events: `module:database AND eventType:(MongoSlowQuery)` (MongoSlowQuery indicates a slow document database query)

**SQL database**:
- SQL database: `module:rdb`
- SQL database events: `module:rdb AND eventType:(MysqlFreeze OR MysqlRecover OR MysqlSlowQuery)` (MysqlFreeze means frozen, MysqlRecover means recovered, and MysqlSlowQuery means a slow query)

**Other services**:
- Workflows: `module:workflow`
- Models: `module:model`
- User permissions: `module:auth`
- LLMs: `module:llm AND logType:llm-tracelog`
- Gateway service calls: `logType:accesslog`
- App publish/delete events: `module:app AND eventType:(AppProdPub OR AppProdDel)` (AppProdPub is a publish event and AppProdDel is a delete event)

These are examples only; adjust the query to the actual log content.

**Note**: To query execution logs for a specific cloud function, prefer `queryFunctions(action="listFunctionLogs", functionName="xxx")`.

service.description:
Log source service:
- `tcb`: Logs from foundational services such as cloud functions, databases, and storage
- `tcbr`: CloudRun container service logs

startTime.description: Query start time in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` format, for example `2024-01-01 00:00:00`.

endTime.description: Query end time in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` format, for example `2024-01-01 23:59:59`.

limit.description: Maximum number of log entries to return; defaults to 20.

context.description: Pagination context used to continue the previous query.

sort.description: Time sort order: `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending.

tools.name: manageLogs
tools.description:
Write entry for the CloudBase logs domain. Enables the CLS log service (aligned with Manager SDK `log.createLogService` / CreateEnvResource Resources=['log']).

**Use cases**:
- Enable CLS log service: `action="createLogService", confirm=true`

Provisioning is asynchronous: API success does not mean the service is immediately ready. Poll with `queryLogs(action="checkLogService")` afterward.

action.description:
Operation type:
- `createLogService`: Enable the CLS log service (requires `confirm=true`)

confirm.description: Explicit confirmation before enabling the log service. Must pass `confirm=true`; omitting it returns CONFIRM_REQUIRED.

tools.name: queryAgents
tools.description: Unified read-only entry for the CloudBase Agents domain. Supports list, detail, and log queries.

tools.name: manageAgents
tools.description: Unified write entry for the CloudBase Agents domain. Supports creating, updating, and deleting remote agents.

tools.name: callCloudApi
tools.description:
Generic Cloud API invocation tool, mainly for CloudBase / Tencent Cloud control-plane and dependent-resource APIs. **Read the API index first** https://docs.cloudbase.net/ai/cloudbase-ai-toolkit/api-reference.md (a daily-synced Action-level index including rate limits; confirm service/Action/params there before calling instead of guessing Action names; for products not covered by the index, check the product's official API docs). If your goal is to integrate CloudBase business APIs such as auth/functions/cloudrun/storage/mysqldb directly over HTTP, prefer the corresponding OpenAPI / Swagger instead of callCloudApi. The existing OpenAPI / Swagger capabilities are not the generic control-plane Action set; for control-plane APIs refer to the CloudBase API overview https://cloud.tencent.com/document/product/876/34809 and the dependent-resource API guide https://cloud.tencent.com/document/product/876/34808. Common tcb Actions by category:

**Env management**: `CreateEnv`, `ModifyEnv`, `DescribeEnvs`, `DestroyEnv`
**User management**: `CreateUser`, `ModifyUser`, `DescribeUserList`, `DeleteUsers`
**Auth config**: `EditAuthConfig`, `DescribeAuthDomains`
**Cloud functions**: `DescribeFunctions`, `CreateFunction`, `UpdateFunctionCode`, `DeleteFunction`
**Database**: `CreateMySQLInstance`, `DescribeMySQLInstances`, `DestroyMySQLInstance`

⚠️ CloudRun (CloudBase Run) must use the tcbr service (CreateCloudRunEnv / CreateCloudRunServer / DescribeEnvBaseInfo / DescribeCloudRunEnvs, version="2022-02-17"); legacy tcb small-tenant APIs such as CreateCloudBaseRunResource are disabled; use manageCloudRun for deploys. Use DescribeEnvBaseInfo (EnvId required) to query a single env's base info / CloudRun provisioning, and DescribeCloudRunEnvs (EnvId optional filter) to query env list / resource info.

⚠️ Region must be passed as the tool-level `region` parameter (mapped to X-TC-Region / regional endpoint), not inside params. Region inside params is stripped and used as the top-level region.

When destroying an env, the common practice is to pass at least `EnvId` and `BypassCheck: true`; if the env is already in quarantine, add `IsForce: true` per the docs.

service.description: Tencent Cloud product identifier. **The value must come from this field's enum allow-list (58 entries)** and determines the request domain https://<service>.tencentcloudapi.com. Values outside the list are rejected; do not invent one. COS is not part of the Cloud API system. See the cloud-api-operations skill for product-to-Action mappings. Always use tcbr for CloudBase Run.

action.description: The exact Action name defined by the official API for the selected service. **If uncertain, consult the official documentation first; do not guess with synonyms or legacy names** (an incorrect guess is reported by the server as action invalid and is difficult to diagnose). See the cloud-api-operations skill for common Actions.

version.description: API version (optional in most cases). Products with **exactly one official version in the allow-list are filled automatically**, so do not pass it. These multi-version products require an explicit version; omitting it returns an error with the available options: tke、mongodb、teo、monitor、vod、sms. Examples: service="tcbr", version="2022-02-17", action="CreateCloudRunEnv", params={EnvId:"env-xxx",PackageType:"Standard"}; service="monitor" requires "2018-07-24" for the alert-policy Action family.

params.description: Parameter object for the Action. Keys must match the official API definition; consult the documentation if uncertain. **Do not put Region here**; use the top-level region parameter for cross-region requests. For CloudBase business APIs, prefer searchKnowledgeBase(mode="openapi") instead of this tool. See the cloud-api-operations skill for examples.

region.description: Cloud API region (X-TC-Region), such as ap-shanghai. Cross-region requests must pass this top-level parameter, not put it in params. ⚠️ ap-singapore exists on both the domestic and international sites. When the site is unspecified, the international site (site=intl) is used. To operate a domestic-site environment in that region, first call auth(action="start_auth", site="domestic") or set TCB_SITE=domestic.

tools.name: prepareFeedback
tools.description:
Return the public repository's new-issue page.

**When to use**:
- `channel="case"`: the work is done and the user wants it on the case wall.
- `channel="retrospective"`: the session went badly and the user wants to report it.

**How to use**:
- Call once. The result is a page URL, not a submitted issue.
- Write the text in the chat and give the user the link. They log in and submit it.
- Do not submit it for them. Do not put an environment ID or secrets in the text.

channel.description: `case` opens the showcase template; `retrospective` opens the retrospective template.

tools.name: queryMessagePush
tools.description: Query Mini Program CloudBase message push config (qbase getappconfig) or all supported message push event constraints (getcallbacksupportlist). Two push modes: cloud function (default, per (msgType,event) callback) and CloudBase Run container (qbase_open=true, receives all messages as a whole payload at the container path). action=list also returns pushMode (cloudfunction|container), containerConfig, callbacks and version; in container mode callbacks may still exist but take no effect (see note); call ensureCloudFunctionMode to switch back before callbacks apply. action=listSupportedEvents returns all supported constraints grouped by message type. Requires the msg-push plugin to be enabled explicitly, plus the WeChat IDE login-state channel (host injects cloudBaseOptions.requestFn).

appid.description: Mini Program AppID (required; must match WeChat DevTools and is used to select the WeChat login-state session)

env.description: Optional environment ID. When provided, list returns only subscriptions for that environment.

action.description:
list: Query the current message push configuration (including pushMode/containerConfig)
listSupportedEvents: Query all supported message push event constraints (grouped by msgType)

tools.name: manageMessagePush
tools.description: Manage Mini Program CloudBase message push config (write ops, requires confirm="yes"). Push modes: cloud function (default, per (msgType,event) callback) vs CloudBase Run container (whole-payload receive; subscribe/unsubscribe/setEnable are rejected in container mode — call ensureCloudFunctionMode first). Declarative idempotency built on read-all → merge → overwrite-all (version optimistic lock). msg_type defaults to "event"; message-type entries use msg_type=text|image|voice|video|miniprogrampage. action=subscribe verifies function_name actually exists in the environment. action=ensureCloudFunctionMode disables container whole-payload receive; action=ensureContainerMode enables it (requires qbase_container_path/qbase_env/text_mode); action=setContainerCallback updates container path/env/text_mode. No write request is made when the set is unchanged (idempotent no-op). Requires the msg-push plugin to be enabled explicitly and the WeChat IDE login-state channel.

appid.description: Mini Program AppID (required; must match WeChat DevTools and is used to select the WeChat login-state session)

env_id.description: Environment ID for the CloudBase environment bound to cloud function subscriptions. It is also the default CloudBase Run environment when ensureContainerMode/setContainerCallback omits qbase_env.

function_name.description: Name of the cloud function that receives message pushes. Used by subscribe/unsubscribe/setEnable/ensureCloudFunctionMode; container-related actions may pass a placeholder.

action.description:
subscribe: Subscribe a specified cloud function (rejected in container mode)
unsubscribe: Remove matching subscriptions (rejected in container mode)
setEnable: Enable or disable matching subscriptions (rejected in container mode)
ensureCloudFunctionMode: Switch to cloud function push mode (disable qbase_open)
ensureContainerMode: Switch to CloudBase Run whole-payload receive (requires qbase_container_path + text_mode)
setContainerCallback: Update the CloudBase Run callback path/env/text_mode

msg_type.description: Message type (defaults to "event"). "event": event entries used with event_types (subscribe may omit it to use the 7 virtual payment events). "text"|"image"|"voice"|"video"|"miniprogrampage": message-type entries whose event is fixed to an empty string; do not pass event_types.

event_types.description: Events to operate on (only when msg_type="event"; query all constraints first with queryMessagePush(action=listSupportedEvents)). subscribe defaults to the 7 virtual payment events when omitted; it is required for unsubscribe / setEnable when msg_type=event.

enable.description: Required for setEnable: true enables the subscription; false disables it.

qbase_container_path.description: CloudBase Run callback path/URL (required for ensureContainerMode; optional update for setContainerCallback)

qbase_env.description: Environment ID hosting the CloudBase Run service (optional for ensureContainerMode/setContainerCallback; defaults to env_id)

text_mode.description: CloudBase Run message body encoding: 1=json, 2=xml (required for ensureContainerMode; optional update for setContainerCallback)

confirm.description: Write confirmation. Pass confirm="yes" to proceed. Omitting it or passing another value returns a pending configuration summary (CONFIRM_REQUIRED); review it and retry. No confirmation is needed when the set is unchanged.
